News.title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked
News.content:
An officer who inappropriately accessed police records more than 2,000 times has been sacked for gross misconduct.

A West Midlands Police misconduct hearing acknowledged PC Shannon Parsons felt "isolated and disconnected" due to working part-time and returning from maternity leave, but had breached standards of professional behaviour.

Parsons had claimed there was a policing purpose to her searches, the panel said, and was seeking to "keep herself up to date, informed and was often in a position to support and assist other colleagues in operational matters".

However, chair of the panel Debra Tedds concluded the searches were carried out for the officer's "own personal benefit".

As a result, Parsons was dismissed without notice and barred from future work in policing.

The searches took part over a period of about five years, the panel heard, and many included incidents near her home address.

Parsons had an otherwise unblemished career in policing in the West Midlands, lasting 13 years, but was said to show no insight or remorse "as to the potential harm that has been caused by accessing the amount of information over a significant time period," according to the panel's report.

News.title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme
News.content:
The BBC says it will pause secondments of government statisticians to its fact checking service, BBC Verify, and review their roles.

Since 2018 the BBC has offered six-month secondment opportunities for up to two civil servant statisticians to work for BBC News's head of statistics.

A BBC spokesperson said: "All BBC journalism and editorial decisions are made by BBC journalists and editors, in line with the BBC's editorial guidelines, so the statisticians never make editorial decisions."

Those currently on secondment would not be involved in the publication of news or content during the review and the current round of recruitment will be paused while the role is reviewed, the corporation added.

The decision follows a report in The Telegraph which said embedded civil servants had been engaging in editorial tasks and raised questions about a breach of impartiality rules.

The spokesperson added that the BBC "takes independence and transparency incredibly seriously, and we must ensure we are meeting the highest standards".

They said although statisticians' work had sometimes been recognised with their names on the BBC website, "they never made editorial decisions".

According to The Telegraph, external, a job advert for the 2027 secondment said a successful candidate would have "the ability to influence decision making, working with credibility and proactively with customers to share knowledge and information".

A now-removed blog post written by one civil servant about their placements showed a secondee describing how they had drafted copy for the news website.

Under the scheme, it is understood that statisticians explain data in writing that can be incorporated into stories, but they do not write the copy itself.

Secondees' contributions can be incorporated into journalism that scrutinises the current government, as well as all political parties.

The seconded statisticians also have to adhere to the Civil Service Code of Practice for Statistics. It requires them to present and use data and statistics objectively and not to withhold or misrepresent data due to political or commercial influence.

News.title: Man arrested after boy, 16, dies in crash
News.content:
A man has been arrested after a 16-year-old boy was killed in a crash in Birmingham.

Police said the teenager was in a white Seat Ibiza which was understood to have hit railings on Shaftmoor Lane at about 20:30 BST on Saturday.

A second passenger, a boy in his teens, was taken to hospital with a serious arm injury.

A 19-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of causing death and serious injury by dangerous driving and failing to provide a breath specimen, West Midlands Police said.

The force stated the 16-year-old boy who lost his life was pronounced dead at the scene, in the Acocks Green area, despite the best efforts of paramedics.

It appealed for information, adding specialist officers from the serious collision investigation unit were asking anyone who had dashcam footage from around the time of the crash to get in touch.

News.title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'
News.content:
An 86-year-old man said learning to read has enabled him to read his and his wife's anniversary cards for the first time in 65 years.

Alan Hannay, from Dibden Purlieu, learned to read through the charity Read Easy, which helps adults across the country who struggle with the skill many of us take for granted.

Hannay told BBC Radio Solent: "It's changed my whole life, my confidence, changed my family life and everything around me.

"It's one of the best experiences I've ever had in my life."

Hannay said he now reads every morning for about an hour and a half and goes to the class twice a week.

"I enjoy it so much now," he said.

The charity said Hannay is an "inspiring example of determination and courage".

It said he asked his local library in Hythe, Southampton, about learning to read, which led him to the charity and his reading coach, Angie.

During his working life as a professional chauffeur, he relied on his memory to drive his clients around London, and at the age of 70 he attended evening classes to improve his reading.

However, he found the group situation difficult.

News.title: House that looks like boulders to be built on moor
News.content:
Plans for a house designed to look like rocks on a famous Yorkshire moor have been approved.

The contemporary structure, which has large irregular-shaped windows and a natural outdoor pool, looks similar to the landmark Cow and Calf Rocks in Ilkley, West Yorkshire.

The house will be built on green belt land which is the garden of a home off Heber's Ghyll Drive, and will be eco-friendly, to an ultra-low energy standard called Passivhaus.

Harrogate-based architects Shaw & Jagger said the scheme was eventually passed by HM Planning Inspectorate through the country house clause, which allows development on green belt for buildings of "exceptional quality".

The architect Matt Masserella-Gill was commissioned to design the home by the landowner David Rasche.

He said the design was "arguably the most complex country house application ever made in this country".

The house has been named Fomorian - meaning a supernatural race of giants in Irish mythology - taking inspiration from the mythical giant Rombald who is told to have lived on Ilkley Moor.

Masserella-Gill said: "The design approach was to propose a scheme that is intrinsically linked to the spirit of its place. Fomorian is of its place, part of the moors, its geology and its spirit.

"We took cues from local folklore, the surrounding rocks; ancient carvings, standing stones and escarpments that are synonymous with the landscape."

News.title: Three officers injured after lorry crashes into police vehicle
News.content:
Three police officers have been injured in County Down after a lorry they were pursuing drove on the wrong side of the road and collided with their vehicle at speed.

A 36-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of driving while unfit through drink or drugs, driving while disqualified and dangerous driving.

A police vehicle was extensively damaged but the officers injuries are thought not to be serious at this time.

The incident began following a report of a blue articulated lorry swerving on Moygannon Road in the Warrenpoint area shortly before 23:30 BST.

"Officers responded and located a lorry matching the description on the Derryleckagh Road, Newry," said Ch Insp Will Brown.

When signalled to stop, the lorry then made off "at speed and on the wrong side of the road", before smashing into a police vehicle and continuing towards Rostrevor.

Brown continued: "The lorry later came to a stop in the Water Street area of Rostrevor where the driver, aged 36, made off on foot but was detained by officers following a short foot chase."

He remains in custody.

Brown said: "Our officers put themselves on the front line to help keep people safe. Thankfully, no one sustained more serious injuries during this incident, including officers and other road users."

News.title: De Zerbi reveals ban in latest bid to lift Spurs spirit: 'You try to find all solutions'
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed a ban he put in place phones during Tottenham’s warm weather training camp in Marbella in his latest attempt to improve the camp’s spirit.

Spurs committed more than £380million on new signings this summer with 10 players joining, but they will start Monday’s home fixture with Coventry at the bottom of the Premier League.

The manager has revealed he banned phones from mealtime during Tottenham’s trip to Marbella.

“We worked on the pitch, we stayed together – we removed phones from breakfast, lunch and dinner to stay together because now it is like (phone) all the time,” De Zerbi told a press conference.

“We had two or three important meetings speaking about football, our situation and how everyone has to take responsibility. And nothing more. There were some dinners just for the players, some dinners just for the staff.

“As a coach you understand you have to improve, you have to change the situation and you try to find all solutions.

“I already did this type of training camp two times with Marseille and it was a good solution. I spoke with the club, with Vinai (Venkatesham), with Johan (Lange), with the owner and together we took the decision, but it’s nothing special.

“It’s just to spend more time together because in pre-season we couldn’t. We had many new players and players who came back from the World Cup. Three or four days together without family, putting the club at the top of their priorities, is normal and is good.”

Asked if players were able to go out independently in Marbella, De Zerbi said: “Yes, with freedom. With no military rules. I love freedom.”

open image in gallery Dejan Kulusevski has been out for an extended period ( Getty )

Fit-again Dejan Kulusevski was part of the Tottenham squad in Spain along with James Maddison, who should face old club Coventry but is yet to start for Spurs since he damaged anterior cruciate ligaments in 2025 and Xavi Simons remains absent with the same injury.

“I am very close with Xavi Simons for example in this moment. I follow him step by step in his journey as an injured player. Like Maddison, because the management of Maddison is totally different. He is another special player and now is available to play,” De Zerbi said.

“Kulusevski was a very important player, even last season when he was injured. It is a part of this job for the players, but at the same time can be a crucial moment to become better, to become stronger.

“You need to play many games to reach the best physical condition but there are players able to be important, even if they play 10, 15 or 20 minutes and James is one player like this.

“Right now he is ready to start the game, but I don’t know if we will start with him. I’m waiting for that moment.”

News.title: Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything surprises at the box office with $15M debut
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A lot of people saw everything in You Can See Everything at movie theaters over the weekend.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s highly anticipated documentary about Theranos scammer Elizabeth Holmes broke box office records during its opening weekend with a staggering $15 million debut from around 850 screens across the U.S. and Canada, more than double of its projected $7 million from its budget of the same amount.

The massive number makes it the biggest opening for a non-musical documentary in more than 20 years, only trailing political documentary Fahrenheit 9/11, which opened with $23.9 million in 2004. It broke the record that was previously set by 2012 nature doc Chimpanzee, which grossed $10.7 million.

You Can See Everything had more than 2,000 sellout showings over the weekend, according to A24, which is in part thanks to its viral marketing campaign and glowing reviews from critics since its surprise world premiere at Telluride Film Festival.

The genre-bending film, which is nearly three hours long, opened in second over the weekend with its limited screenings. Paramount’s video game adaptation Street Fighter came out on top with $31 million. 20th Century Studios survival thriller Whalefall followed in third place, grossing a disappointing $8 million.

open image in gallery Nathan Fielder and 'Primetime' director Lance Oppenheim collaborated on 'You Can See Everything' ( JC Olivera/Getty Images )

open image in gallery Nathan Fielder’s documentary follows Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks before she goes to prison in 2023 ( A24 )

You Can See Everything, which was produced in secret over three years, follows Holmes in the weeks before she started her 11-year prison sentence in 2023 for defrauding investors with her medical tech company.

Holmes and her partner, California hotel heir Billy Evans, asked A24 to intimately film their life with their two children before she surrendered to her life behind bars.

Fielder, an absurdist comedian known for his shows Nathan For You and The Rehearsal, took on the project alongside Primetime director Oppenheim.

“I am still struggling to this day to understand what I went through,” Fielder said in a New York Film Festival Q&A session after the screening.

The film has received heaps of critical acclaim, achieving a rare 99 percent score on Rotten Tomatoes, with some calling it the “film of the year,” while others speculate that the film could nab the first-ever Best Picture nomination for a documentary at this year’s Academy Awards.

It has been a huge year for A24. After Marty Supreme opened in December 2025 as the company’s highest-grossing release ever, Backrooms quickly broke that record this summer by grossing more than $400 million on a $10 million budget.

News.title: What sparked the fiery protests in France – and how they could spread across Europe
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Hundreds of people were arrested and buildings set on fire across France on Saturday as protests over the cost of living crisis spread.

In Paris, police fired tear gas into crowds on Saturday, while there were also violent incidents reported in Marseille, Rennes, Toulouse and Angers. By Sunday, as the clean-up began, more than 2,000 people had been arrested.

The turmoil marks the latest test for Emmanuel Macron’s presidency as France contends with both foreign and domestic troubles.

The protests began in September, launched by students angry at the conditions at their high schools after the summer holidays.

However, they have since grown, fuelled by a wider group of protesters incensed about the cost of living.

Here’s everything you need to know about the movement.

Where the protests began

open image in gallery Students march to protest against under-resourced schools in Rennes, France, on 13 October ( AP )

Demonstrations first erupted in September in a high school in Creteil, southeast of Paris, over a lack of staff.

From there, class strikes, blockades and demonstrations spread to other Paris suburbs and then nationwide, even in smaller towns. Hundreds of schools had to close because of damage or attacks on staff.

High schoolers said they had grievances over schools that are under-resourced, with dilapidated facilities and insufficient staff, notably in lower-income neighborhoods. French media showed videos of scampering rats, collapsed ceilings, leaks, broken furniture and other woes in dilapidated schools.

Some students also complained that during summer heat waves, they roast in classrooms without air-conditioning, while in winter they freeze. They say school days, which often run from 8am-6pm, are too exhausting and the university entrance system is complex and unfair. Some university students also joined the protests.

There have been broader concerns in France that the country's education system is losing ground to other countries and failing in its mission to enable children from disadvantaged backgrounds to move up the social ladder. Scores in reading comprehension and mathematics have plunged, according to the latest PISA report, which evaluates students worldwide.

Why protests exploded on Saturday

open image in gallery A protester holds a French flag in front of Lyon's tourism office, which was set on fire on Saturday ( AFP/Getty )

Demonstrations were boosted by other groups on Saturday, protesting the high cost of living and what they say is the deterioration of the social welfare system.

The General Confederation of Labour (CGT), which is one of the country’s largest unions, backed the protests, issuing a call for lower prices and higher pensions and wages.

Tens of thousands of people took to the streets. Protesters in Marseille stormed the town hall, painting an ‘A’ for anarchy on a wall, while in Paris, police fired tear gas and a water cannon and rioters threw stones and fireworks.

In Lyon, protesters set fire to the city’s tourism office.

French authorities said there were more than 500,000 protesters across the country, with more than 800 arrests in Paris alone.

Mr Macron has called for calm, saying “we all feel anger and shame” after “unprecedented violence” nationwide. He vowed to “make examples if need be” of the rioters, warning for “those who want to spark violence and create unrest in our country, we will not yield”.

Police response to students has drawn ire

open image in gallery A protest against under-resourced schools in Paris on 8 October ( AP )

Riot police have liberally used tear gas and wielded their batons to disperse crowds during the student protests. Police made more than 6,600 arrests nationwide as of last week, an unusually high number for a French protest movement.

A police tear gas grenade shattered a 14-year-old’s jaw and many of his teeth. A 15-year-old lost a hand in an incident involving a police stun grenade. Other adolescents have also suffered life-changing injuries blamed on police weaponry during protests.

Police and school staff have been targeted with powerful fireworks and other injury-causing projectiles. The interior ministry says acid has been hurled in some cases, and that people intent on destruction and looting have grafted themselves onto the high schoolers’ movement.

Presidential candidates are seizing the moment

open image in gallery French president Emmanuel Macron ( Reuters )

Candidates campaigning to succeed Mr Macron in a coming presidential election in April and May have seized on the demonstrations as a political issue. Mr Macron is constitutionally barred from seeking a third consecutive term.

Far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has positioned himself firmly on the side of the students and has decried police actions. His party invited high school activists on stage at a rally Sunday, then proposed lowering the voting age to 16 and scrapping selective admissions at universities.

Meanwhile, far-right leader Marine Le Pen has called for broader police powers against rioters. Conservative former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe, one of Le Pen’s main challengers for the presidency, has condemned those who “break things, burn things or assault people.”

Other European countries have seen unrest

Taking grievances to the streets is hardly unusual in the country that spawned the French Revolution of 1789. To name just a few, there were mass student protests in 1968, weeks of suburban unrest in 2005, yellow vest protests in 2018-2019, and demonstrations in 2023 against raising the retirement age.

But some other countries have also seen some student unrest.

In neighboring Belgium, some schools closed in Liege, a day after violence in the city and arrests there.

Several Italian cities also saw student protests last week, though on a smaller scale than in France and focused on a broader set of domestic grievances. On Saturday there was a protest in Milan where rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire, emptying Piazza del Duomo and a luxury shopping arcade when the area would usually be teeming with shoppers.

The march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully. But masked protesters threw stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and set fire to barricades made from bar tables. Images of the aftermath showed a severely damaged carabinieri car.

Police used water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowds. At least two police officers were injured and about 50 demonstrators, including many minors, were detained, the LaPresse news agency reported.

News.title: Private jet skids off runway, hits fence at Las Vegas airport
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A private jet went off the end of a runway during a planned takeoff at Las Vegas' main airport Sunday and hit a perimeter fence, officials said.

No injuries were reported in the 11 a.m. mishap at Harry Reid International Airport, said airport spokesperson Monika Bertaki. She didn't say what caused the plane, a Dassault Falcon 50, to go off the runway.

Two runways were closed for inspection after the incident and the Federal Aviation Administration temporarily paused planned flights to the airport, causing delays.

As of August, the airport had over 370,000 operations and more than 34 million passengers so far in 2026.

___

Wilder is a corps member for The Associated Press/Report for America Statehouse News Initiative. Report for America is a nonprofit national service program that places journalists in local newsrooms to report on undercovered issues.

News.title: The Archers features first lesbian wedding in its 75-year history
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Archers has featured the first lesbian wedding.

Pip Archer and Stella Pryor have married in the long-running radio series, marking the first lesbian wedding in the BBC Radio 4 drama's 75-year history.

The ceremony took place during a “horrendous” storm in Sunday's episode of the long-running programme.

Pryor, who is voiced by Lucy Speed, declared her love for her new wife through tears as she made her vows.

The character said: “Whatever happens, we will weather it and I can promise you that I will do my very best to protect you from the worst of the storms that life throws at us.

“To look after you and your lovely girl Rosie the best I possibly can. To support you and adore you.

“My ultimate goal is to give you the happiest of lives, because you’re my universe Pip, and I couldn’t love you more.

“I cannot wait to be your wife.”

Archer, voiced by Daisy Badger, followed with her own vows.

She said: “I’m nervous – Stella just made me cry. That was so beautiful.

“Stella, my life is so much better and so much more interesting because of you.

“You excite me, you challenge me, but you ground me too and keep me on the straight and narrow, even though you’re not straight – and turns out nor am I.”

Reflecting on their relationship, which began in 2023, she continued: “You were my friend, and then my girlfriend, and in a few minutes you’ll be my wife.

“Meeting you is like coming home, and I promise now in front of our beloved friends and family I will love you forever and ever.”

open image in gallery Carole Boyd, Ben Norris and Sunny Ormonde perform a scene as Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall listens during a celebration of ‘The Archers’ 70th anniversary at Clarence House on December 7, 2021 in London, England ( Getty )

The episode opened with farmer Archer having her hair styled by Chelsea Horrobin.

Talk turned to the weather, and the pair joked about having “hair that can withstand a hurricane”, which prompted a tribute to singer Dolly Parton and a memory of her signature sky-high and platinum-blonde wigs.

The country music superstar died on August 25 aged 80 after suffering from cancer.

Having remembered how “the whole world seemed so sad when she died”, Archer and Pryor agreed their wedding was “going to be memorable” given the weather.

Elsewhere, Eddie Grundy and his wife Clarrie had to give up their journey to the ceremony after noticing the roof of their pole barn coming loose in the storm, and went to check their beloved turkeys instead.

They missed the nuptials as a result.

After the ceremony, Tony Turner's character Vince Casey and hairdressing student Horrobin braved the storm to clear the road.

The episode closed on a cliffhanger, with a tree apparently falling on Horrobin.

Listeners will have to wait until 7pm on Monday to find out what happens next.

The wedding comes two decades after The Archers aired its first gay ceremony, when Andrew Wincott's character Adam Macy and Ian Craig, voiced by Stephen Kennedy, entered into a civil partnership in 2006.

That couple married in 2015.

The radio drama made headlines earlier this week after stars including Dame Judi Dench urged the BBC to keep recording the programme in Birmingham.

The appeal followed the corporation's decision to scrap plans for a bespoke studio at its Tea Factory site in Digbeth amid cost-cutting measures.

The BBC is instead considering existing studios around the UK, raising concerns that the show could be recorded outside Birmingham for the first time since 1951.

News.title: The bombshells from the undercover sting operation which has plunged Reform into crisis
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nigel Farage’s party has been plunged into crisis after an undercover sting operation revealed racist, sexual, and violent rhetoric among its members.

Several Reform UK members have been suspended or resigned as the party faces intense scrutiny over the fresh revelations.

It has been accused of “appalling behaviour” and “extreme racism” following footage released from an undercover investigation called Undercover: A Year in Reform by ITV Exposure, screened on Sunday night.

The year-long investigation goes inside the heart of Reform UK’s political operations, and follows election candidates and councillors across England and Wales during the May local elections and four by-election campaigns in 2025 and 2026.

Here is everything we know so far.

open image in gallery Nigel Farage was caught letting of a mayoral candidate accused of racism ( ITV )

Mayoral candidate accused of using racist slur against David Lammy

The Reform leader has been accused of protecting his party’s mayoral candidate for Hampshire and the Solent, Chris Parry, who made a social media post saying the then-deputy prime minister should “go home to the Caribbean”.

Secretly filmed footage shows Mr Farage telling his director of communications, Ed Sumner, that Mr Parry must apologise, before Mr Sumner accused the Reform leader of “protecting him”.

Mr Farage responds: “It’s showing a bit of... bit of sorrow. Look, ‘I’m sorry’ is probably a good thing to hear. Just take the f***ing deal.”

When Mr Farage left, Mr Sumner was caught saying: “He’s lucky, if it was up to me, I’d have kicked him out f***ing months ago.”

Mr Parry was later suspended after he appeared to liken a Jewish neighbourhood watch group to “Islamists on horseback” following an arson attack on Jewish community ambulances.

open image in gallery Alan Feeney has resigned after he was recorded calling Asian families ‘parasites’ ( ITV )

Reform councillors and candidates made racist and sexist remarks

Undercover journalists have secretly filmed Reform councillors making a series of racist, sexist, and violent remarks.

Councillor Alan Feeney in Solihull, who has since resigned, was recorded saying that the area had been “infested” with Asian families, who he referred to as “absolute parasites”.

Mr Feeney also said of Asian people: “Drag them out of their homes, stick them on planes and f*** them off to Pakistan.”

Chris Whelan, a Reform election candidate in Solihull, said of a female Reform candidate: “If she was my daughter, it would still be bath night on a Thursday. I’ll wash you properly this time.” He also resigned from Reform for personal and health reasons.

open image in gallery Several councillors and candidates have been exposed in the investigation ( ITV )

Dean Miller, a Reform councillor for Bromley, said of illegal immigrants crossing the Channel: “I’d get nicked for saying what I would do. Do you know what I mean? I’ll take them out bruv, I don’t care… the way I see it, you’ve got to kill or you’re going to be killed... These f***ers have come to rape and pillage and f***ing kill us. There’s no doubt about it.”

He was also filmed undercover calling for King Charles to be beheaded.

“Apparently King Charles is a f***ing Muslim… someone from the inside saw a f***ing prayer mat and all that in one of his f***ing rooms … I think that’s f***ing traitorous,” he said.

Mr Miller also resigned following the investigation and now sits as an independent councillor, according to ITV.

Speaking about children he claimed had vandalised shops in the area, he said: “It’s just like all the ethnic f***ing kids, like they’re not white, they’re all f***ing Black and they’re like f***ing animals. It’s horrible to say it, I’m not racist, but you know what I mean.”

An aspiring Reform MP also told an undercover ITV reporter that “concentration camps” should be built for asylum seekers who arrive in small boats to the UK. They have since been suspended from the party.

open image in gallery Sarah Pochin described Reform as ‘chauvinisitic’ ( ITV )

MP Sarah Pochin said the party was ‘f***ing chauvinistic’

The Runcorn and Helsby MP was caught telling an undercover female reporter that senior party officials “just exclude you if you are a woman”.

“I go out on all the shows, and go: ‘Oh no, it’s lovely, oh they’re all so welcoming.’ Shit… they just exclude you if you’re a woman… It’s really tough being a girl with all of this alpha male shit going on,” she said.

Reform’s treasury spokesperson, Robert Jenrick, insisted the party was not chauvinistic and also denied Reform’s vetting processes were biased, but said: “All political parties have bad apples.”

In a statement, Reform said: “Reform UK has improved and prioritised its vetting procedures, but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting.

“This is the same for all organisations. However good the vetting, one cannot vet a future comment.

“There is no room for racism in Reform UK. We always respect due process of investigations, and whilst these are ongoing, it would not be appropriate to comment on individual cases.”

Undercover: A Year in Reform aired on Sunday 18 October at 10.20pm on ITV1, ITVX, STV and STV Player.

News.title: Flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna forced to make emergency landing after bomb threat
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A plane flying from Tel Aviv to Vienna was forced to make an emergency landing in Sofia on Sunday evening after a bomb threat.

Bulgarian state television reported the diversion, which saw the aircraft come down in the capital.

The broadcaster BNT said the threat was made against the flight, which was carrying 51 passengers and six crew members. It cited a statement from the transportation ministry in its reporting.

According to BNT, a crew member on board reported receiving the threat. An air force fighter jet then escorted the plane until it landed.

Bulgaria's defense ministry said fighter jets responded after the threat was reported on the Airbus A320.

The airline operating the flight has not been identified.

The incident follows increase tension on flights to and from Israel after an apparent attempted hijack last month.

The flydubai aircraft, flight FZ1073, was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for emergency use, according to reports.

The captain has since described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.

open image in gallery Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, meets Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national and flydubai pilot who is under treatment after he was stabbed by a colleague aboard a plane ( Reuters )

Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as ⁠a hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, helping to thwart what the UAE attorney general has said was an attempted suicide attack by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport.

Speaking ⁠in an interview with The National ​newspaper ⁠from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, his head and left arm bandaged, Machchhar said that when the first blow landed, he thought something had ⁠gone "horribly wrong the aircraft structure", before quickly realising he was being attacked and things had "taken ​a ⁠drastic turn".

"The next thought was ‌I need to get help in here," he said in the interview published on Saturday.

"My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts and I ‌tried to just block the blows as much ‌as I could," he said, pointing to his arm that was wounded as he defended himself. "The blows were coming on the head."

"Immediately my hand went to the knob which opens the door and screaming ⁠for my colleagues, screaming his name."

"I believe that was the first time when I lost my consciousness."

The incident caused the airliner to plunge 16,000 feet (4,900 meters) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were on board landed ‌the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect, an Omani national, was transferred ​to the UAE, flydubai's home country.

Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming "between my colleague and the ‌guy".

He said the scariest ​thing he felt was the aircraft ‌nose "steeply going down."

News.title: Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City
News.content:
In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough
News.content:
Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

News.title: Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation
News.content:
Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

Sports.title: What is wrong with Bruno Fernandes? Carrick tries to throw fans off scent as concerns over Man Utd captain grow
Sports.content:
Next

BRUNO FERNANDES is in a funk – no matter how much boss Michael Carrick tries to throw us off the scent.

The Old Trafford skipper was a shell of himself again during Manchester United‘s third straight 1-1 Premier League draw.



Carrick, however, insisted it was business as usual, projecting calm as the public face of the club after a rocky week dominated by Lisandro Martinez‘s outburst.

Carrick said: “No, he’s all right, no, it’s not a big deal. He is absolutely fine.”



But Carrick also said United’s sixth game without a win was a “fresh start” for the club hitting 13th in the table, with two wins from ten.

And he was even further off the mark when he said it had been a “quiet week inside the squad,” despite Martinez’s apology for lashing out at the board for failing to invest in the summer.



Man Utd ratings v Leeds MAN UTD went six games without a win after a 1-1 draw with rivals Leeds United. Bryan Mbeumo’s 35th minute goal was cancelled out by Dominic Calvert-Lewin swiftly after the break. Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the United players at Elland Road.

Twice this week Carrick has spoken of a Fernandes “injury niggle” but stressed there was nothing to worry about.

But their talisman’s performances before and since have suggested otherwise.

Yet Carrick again kept the out-of-sorts club captain on until the final whistle for the seven successive league games this season.

The mention of an injury was perhaps an attempt to deflect the mounting scrutiny facing the reigning Prem player of the season.

The 32-year-old was crowned the best of the best in the scrutinised league in the world, chalking up 21 assists to break the all-time record held by Thierry Henry and Kevin de Bruyne.

Yet at the start of what was meant to be a new United era, the midfielder’s form has become an unexpected problem for Carrick, an avatar of where United stand.

Anybody with eyes can see that Fernandes is well off it.

He has gone five Prem matches without scoring or assisting – his longest run since April-May 2025.

Carrick denied that his positional changes, with Fernandes being shunted to the right wing in the 2-0 loss at Atletico Madrid midweek and as a false nine at Leeds, have affected his mood or form. But he would say that.



Kobbie Mainoo’s injury has prompted a reshuffle, pushing Youri Tielemans into Fernandes’ preferred No 10 role while new signings Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba lined up in midfield.

Tielemans has enjoyed his best week since joining after facing criticism for his ability to cover ground from deep during the first eight games.

The fact Fernandes stayed on all match is a concern, a sign that Carrick is forcing square pegs into round holes to keep him on the pitch.

Carrick said: “He was through the middle today and played a slightly different position in midweek, but apart from that, it’s pretty much as usual.



“He’s an important part of our team. He has been for us for some time, and that’s not changing.

“There was a freshness to the group. You look at the midfield with Carlos and Andrey, that’s a pretty fresh spine of the team, through the middle of the pitch. Both young players are adapting to life at this football club. They were terrific today.”

Yet a five-minute compilation could be made of all of Fernandes’ head-loss moments at Elland Road.

Booked on 17 minutes for mouthing off at ref Darren England after a late challenge on Leeds star Tarik Muharemovic, the hot-head kept sulking.



He went through the full spectrum at Elland Road. Hands on face. Hands on head. Hands on hips, complaining and kicking off.

Daniel Farke’s players clocked on: the more tackles they made, the more United’s captain would combust.

There was still time for one final Fernandes complaint, as he screamed into the Yorkshire air after a stepover didn’t come off late on.

United have long tolerated his on-pitch petulance, but his dedication had never faced serious scrutiny—until now.

There is a suggestion that he appears fed up with false promises made by the club’s recruitment department and ambition shown in the summer.



The club captain, entering his final year with a club-held option to extend it by a year, is in a contract stalemate.

He has stepped back from press duties to dodge mounting speculation over his Old Trafford future. He would be right to question the direction of the club.

Eagle-eyed fans caught him failing to celebrate United’s goal against Spurs last Saturday before he left Old Trafford in hurry with reporters still waiting for Carrick’s press conference.

The under-pressure boss faces a defining dilemma over whether to drop him.

If that gamble backfires, Carrick leaves himself dangerously exposed to an even greater backlash.

Sports.title: Former Premier League club’s abandoned 30,000-capacity stadium now used as an allotment following demolition
Sports.content:
Next

SWANSEA are dreaming of a stunning return to the Premier League – but their former home is now unrecognisable.

The Welsh side are top of the Championship despite suffering a 1-0 defeat to fellow promotion chasers West Ham on Saturday.



They set a new attendance record at the Swansea.com Stadium when 20,973 fans turned up to see the showdown with the Hammers, who were relegated from the top-flight on the final day of last season.

But the Swans’ beloved Vetch Field, which they walked away from in May 2005, has been given a huge makeover.



Parts of the abandoned arena have remained intact for more than two decades – including the pitch’s original centre circle and players’ tunnel.

And some of the land where Vetch Field once stood has been transformed into an allotment following the demolition of the stadium.



It has allowed Swansea fans to grow vegetables where they once saw club legends spearheading their side to wins.

The decision was made to put together a community garden despite initial plans being drawn up to build four blocks of flats.

Vetch Field closed its gates for the final time when Swansea notched a 2-1 win over Welsh rivals Wrexham in the FAW Premier Cup final.

And the Swans posted their record attendance at the stadium – with more than 30,000 supporters flocking to see an FA Cup defeat to Arsenal in February 1968.

Sports.title: Noni Madueke hails Arsenal for showing ‘a champion’s spirit’ in Nottingham Forest win
Sports.content:

NONI MADUEKE hailed Arsenal for showing a “champion’s spirit” to squeeze past Nottingham Forest.

The winger came off the bench and was the Gunners’ hero by scoring the winner with 10 minutes to go.



The goal was Arsenal’s only shot on target – but Madueke loved the way the reigning champs ground out a 1-0 win to keep pace with Manchester City.

The England forward said: “We showed grit, determination and a champion’s spirit – I’m really pleased.



“At times maybe last year this game might not have gone for us as it did at the end. We have that extra belief, that extra mentality now.

“We know we are the champions and we can pull it out of the bag wherever we go. I’m just delighted we were able to do that.



“The Premier League can shock you – we had a shock versus Brighton and it was up to us to get back to the drawing board, regroup, go again and show everyone why we are the champs.”

Arteta was delighted with Madueke’s impact after bringing him on at half time for Eberechi Eze.

Madueke ultimately made the difference and his deflected strike off defender Jair Cunha meant Arsenal won to close the gap on Prem leaders City to three points.

Arteta said: “Noni is just a special guy. I saw an interview where they were asking a few of our players who would you call if you have a problem?



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“And some of them said Noni, which I was surprised by. It’s a massive credit and explains the kind of person that he is.

“After the international break he has been showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well in his actions and he’s becoming more decisive in matches.”

This was the third Prem game in a row where a player has come off the bench to score the winner for Arsenal and Arteta is thrilled by his substitutes contributing so much.

He said: “At the end I had the belief that the physical level [of Forest] was going to drop.

“The ‘finishers’ delivered because the game changed and the context of that game changed a little bit.”



The victory was also Arsenal’s third win on the spin since City were found guilty by the Premier League for breaching financial rules.

The Gunners have kept pace with them since then and Arteta is pleased the verdict has not led to his players taking their eye off the ball.

He said: “Now it’s three wins after that defeat at Brighton. We’re in a good place. But we can always improve and we should improve.”

Ilett has vowed not to cut his hair until the Red Devils win five consecutive games – a feat looking more unlikely by the week.



United have had FIVE managers since the challenge began, with Ilett‘s trim first being reliant on Erik Ten Hag‘s team.





After Ten Hag failed to win five in a row, interim Ruud van Nistelrooy managed to win two consecutive games but wasn’t given the chance to complete the streak before Ruben Amorim took over.

And finally, it’s Michael Carrick who could finally get Ilett a very much needed trim.

The Gunners’ finishers helped them get the job done against Nottingham Forest and credit needs to go to Noni Madueke.

This was a pretty worrying performance for Arsenal – just one shot on target in the whole game, and there were similar sort of questions and performances to what we saw at times last season.

Sports.title: NFL issues statement on Paris game after violent protests in France ahead of New Orleans Saints vs Pittsburgh Steelers

THE NFL has been forced to issue a statement on next Sunday’s proposed Paris game after riots in the city.

Police arrested around 1,800 people after 550,000 people took to the streets for protests which turned violent.



Shopfronts were shattered and cars were burnt out as people protested over rising costs of living and deteriorating public services.

It came just a week before the NFL is due to stage a game in the city for the first time ever.



The New Orleans Saints will face the Pittsburgh Steelers in a Week 7 clash at the Stade de France.

And Saturday night’s events in Paris forced the NFL to issue a statement.

It read, “Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday.

“We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters.

“We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.”

The Saints will travel to Paris right after their game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.



New Orleans will spend the entire week in France, while the Steelers plan to leave America on Thursday.

Saints spokesperson Greg Bensel said, “In addition to working closely with the NFL, we have also maintained daily security updates with our security partners in France.

The defending champions didn’t have their shooting boots on until Madueke‘s wicked deflected strike hit the target and went in past Matz Sels in the 80th minute – their first shot on target.



The hosts had had the lion’s share of the chances but were unable to make them count with David Raya never truly tested, though the likes of Gabriel Magalhaes needed to be on top form to preserve the clean sheet.

But he was subbed midway through the second half as Arteta rang the changes, replacing him with the competitor for his place, Jurrien Timber.

Ezri Konsa – 8

Prince William described him as a ‘Rolls Royce’ at Aston Villa and he has taken that reputation with him to Arsenal. Showed from the start that Liam Delap would not be getting things all his own way before a superb late tackle on the £50million striker.

He was definitely not afraid to make his physical presence tell – but he was nutmegged by Murillo in stoppage time.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Gabriel Magalhaes – 8

Looked composed at the back against a Forest side who had not scored at home before today this season.

Continued to play a leading role in Willam Saliba’s absence and went close to scoring before Madueke found the net.

Riccardo Calafiori – 6

Made some early mistakes but quick to put things right when he could.

It was a day when outstanding individual performances were few and far between, but he played his part in what could be a crucial three points for Arsenal.



Declan Rice – 6

Made life difficult for Forest first, but some mistakes allowed Oliver Glasner’s side some rare sights on goal, and he escaped a booking when he needed some strong-arm tactics to bring down Delap.

Flat at times but produced a crucial late challenge to prevent a Forest leveller.

Bruno Guimaraes – 6

Some nice early touches left Forest standing, and he was prepared to take one for the team when he was flattened by a first half free kick.



Tidied up nicely at the back then he was needed but could not make an impression.

Martin Odegaard – 7

Saw plenty of the ball, but Forest putting numbers in his way meant he was frustrated.

Produced some telling passes though as he looked for a way through but stuck to his task and the skipper remained an influential figure

Found little space during the game but when his crosses came in, there was often nobody on the end of them as Forest defended superbly.

Made little impact for much of the game, but he was not the only one.



Eberechi Eze – 3

Produced a nervy display in his first Premier League start of the season.

He simply did not take the chance he was given out left, and Mikel Arteta had seen enough when he made a pass to no-one in first half stoppage time. That was his last action and he was subbed at the break

Looked anonymous for the first half, one off-target header saw him cut a frustrated figure up front before finding the side netting.

Most accurate hit was an arm in the face of Xaver Schlager. Arteta wants 25 goals from him this season, but that looks a long way off.

Came on at half-time and showed how it was done. He replaced the disappointing Eze and produced the winner with a deflected shot off Jair Cunha that gave him his first Premier League goal of the season.

He was right to milk the support of the Arsenal fans who must have thought they would have to settle for a point.

Came on for the latter stages and found himself tested by Forest sub Callum Hudson-Odoi late in the game.

Sports.title: Neville delivers Carrick warning after Man Utd 'stepping stone' performance
Sports.content:
Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville believes Manchester United's 1-1 draw at Leeds could be a "stepping stone" but has warned that Michael Carrick will have a problem if his side are still 13th in the Premier League come January.

United have just seven points from seven league matches, winning just one of those, which is their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight season for 40 years.

Despite extending their winless run in all competitions to six games with the draw at Elland Road, the performance was much improved, with Carrick's tactical tweaks making his side more compact and defensively solid.

Neville agreed with the United head coach's assessment that Sunday's performance at Elland Road was a step in the right direction.

Speaking on the Gary Neville podcast, the Sky Sports pundit said: "[There's] a depressed standard and a low expectation right now.

"But it'll feel like a stepping stone for Michael Carrick, and it'll feel like the first step on the ladder in the Premier League.

"They may take some confidence from that, and there might be a blueprint there. Maybe we have to bring Matheus Cunha, Marcus Rashford and others off the bench, and we might just have to have a go at being more solid."

'Carrick's got a problem if Man Utd 13th in January'

Image: Man Utd have just one win from seven Premier League matches

United's paltry points return has them sitting 13th in the Premier League after seven games, already five points adrift of fifth place, which was enough for Champions League qualification last season.

Neville says there is no need for panic just yet but feels United have to show signs of improvement over the next few weeks otherwise Carrick could find himself in hot water come the new year.

"I would say fourth would be a birdie, fifth would be par, and sixth would be a bogey," said Neville of his former club's targets for the season. "But they can't finish outside the top five, because then you're missing out on Champions League and it becomes a vicious circle.

"Then you can't get those players because they want to play in the Champions League and you can't get the money from it and you've lost the £60m-£70m and you're in the Europa League on Thursday nights.

"Fifth is a must for Michael Carrick to continue to grow and Manchester United continue to grow with investment.

"If they're 13th in January, he's got a problem because then you are what you are. Whereas I think it's still early enough, seven points from seven games, to say, 'okay, still early in the season'. You can't say that after 15 games.

"It has to change in the next few weeks: Bournemouth is really important and Chelsea away. And how he manages the games in between that.

"You've got to say fifth. You know that anything less than fifth is going to be a disappointment and a dropping standard from the start of the season where everybody expected them to finish.

"And at the moment, they're well short of that because you look at Brighton, Liverpool, Aston Villa - they look like they're picking up a little bit. It's difficult."

'Baleba staying fit is going to be critical'

Image: Carlos Baleba made his Man Utd debut against Tottenham

Neville has seen encouraging signs from Carlos Baleba's start to life as a Manchester United player and feels the midfielder staying fit is crucial for Carrick this season.

Signed from Brighton for £70m at the end of the summer window, the 21-year-old arrived with an ankle injury that has kept him from featuring until he came on in the second half of last Saturday's 1-1 draw against 10-man Tottenham.

Baleba has started the last two games, at Atletico Madrid and Leeds, and brought an added steel to United's midfield alongside fellow summer-signing Andrey Santos.

"I know he had a difficult season last year at Brighton, but you watch him in his first couple of games or so for United, and he's got something," said Neville. "He's got a bit of strength about him, he's got a presence.

"Him staying fit is gonna be absolutely critical, I can understand why Michael Carrick took him off with 20 minutes to go [at Leeds], because he's played [nearly] three games in a week.

"Maybe he doesn't play him against Como on Wednesday. We're not throwing the Champions League away, but Manchester United have to beat Bournemouth next weekend.

"I just wonder whether that Santos-Baleba partnership is going to stay there for a bit, and let a couple of [the attacking players] float around in front, and be a lot more solid, make sure we're not giving as much space away.

"I'm sick of Manchester United's team being easy to play against, and Michael Carrick will be sick of it."

Sports.title: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
Sports.content:
Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.

After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.

However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

The result takes Arsenal to 18 points, three behind leaders Manchester City. For Forest, the frustration deepens. They drop into the relegation zone and are still waiting for their first home league goal of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Noni Madueke's deflected strike gives Arsenal the lead

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Murillo goes close against Arsenal

Analysis: Eze must prove his worth as Arsenal's main man after Madueke shines

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

Eberechi Eze has spent a year at Arsenal since leaving Crystal Palace, but questions remain over whether he is ready to become one of the club's leading figures as their ambitions continue to grow.

His talent is undeniable. The real concern is whether he can influence games consistently, and the trip to Nottingham Forest presented another opportunity to silence his doubters.

With Arsenal struggling to break down Forest, Eze had the chance to make a difference. Instead, he was substituted at half-time, watching from the sidelines as Noni Madueke replaced him and went on to score the 80th-minute winner.

Roy Keane's assessment on Sky Sports was telling, suggesting his concerns extended beyond a single performance.

"We're still waiting for him, the talent is there," Keane said. "We just want him to be at Arsenal and be able to take responsibility and try to be the main man at a big club."

That is the challenge facing Eze. At Crystal Palace, he was the focal point, the player expected to create chances and turn games in his team's favour. At Arsenal, however, talent alone will not earn him that status. He must deliver consistently, particularly in tight contests when his team need inspiration.

Ian Wright offered some important context, describing Eze as a "moments player" who benefits from having players around him and can become isolated on the left.

There is merit to that argument. Eze offers a different threat to Madueke, whose pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders gave Arsenal a fresh dimension in the second half.

Yet that only underlines the challenge facing the former Palace man. While Madueke seized his opportunity and made an immediate impact, Eze failed to leave his mark on the contest.

Competition for places is healthy at a club with Arsenal's ambitions. For Eze, though, the task is no longer simply to showcase his ability in flashes. He must demonstrate that he can influence games regularly, take responsibility when his team need him and establish himself as a first-choice player.

The talent is there. Now, Eze must prove he can turn that potential into consistent performances and become one of Arsenal's main men.

Forest's lack of goals has caught up with them

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

There was only so long Nottingham Forest could rely on defensive resilience before their lack of goals caught up with them. Now they are in the relegation zone.

Oliver Glasner's side have failed to score in every Premier League home game this season, and their defeat to Arsenal highlighted why they are in trouble.

Forest competed and created opportunities, but lacked the quality in the final third to make their efforts count.

Liam Delap struggled to make an impact against Arsenal's defence, summing up a frustrating afternoon. Forest needed someone to take responsibility, but their attacking play lacked conviction.

That is the worry for Glasner. Defensive organisation can only take a team so far; they still need goals to win matches.

Forest are now in the relegation zone with just five points. Their performances offer some encouragement, but until they find a reliable source of goals at the City Ground, it is difficult to see their situation improving.

90+2: Murillo nearly equalises - The defender drives forward and curls narrowly wide.

90+3: Konsa saves Arsenal - The defender times a vital challenge to deny Delap.

Arteta: We knew margins would be small

Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"We did something we didn't do in the two seasons before and that is win the game.

"We knew the margins would be small unless you open up the game much earlier, which we had two chances to do.

"The longer the game goes on, they have more belief and that's when you have to take more risks and that when the game can break.

"But we talked about it. We had to be so patient, without getting frustrated.

"It was tough to generate open chances against them. And we have to take them when we get them.

"We had another three chances [in the gme] that should have been on target.

"And not only on target, but they should have been goal.

"That's the difference, you have to be clinical."

Glasner: Have to take your chances against the champions

Oliver Glasner to Sky Sports:

"I think everybody feels the result is unfair today (in terms of the way we performed).

"But it's another defeat and another game when we couldn't score at the City Ground.

"But the performance today, especially defensively was of the top level.

"It was their only shot on target (that Arsenal scored from) and this one was deflected and Arsenal took the win.

"We also had our moments and it's important when you play the champions you take your moments.

"But today, the performance, effort, spirit and energy we had was on a very good level. But the result is frustrating."

Sports.title: Texans beat Jags in final seconds of Wembley thriller
Sports.content:
Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked a 49-yard field goal as time expired to lift the Houston Texans to a 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in a thriller at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.

It was a game that began with referee Larry Smith being carted off with a non-contact injury in the opening seconds. A game that spent its interval staging on-field Corgi races. And a game that concluded with another dose of boot-fuelled drama following Cam Little's last-second winner against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham the previous week.

Texans quarterback CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns while Jaylin Noel led his side with four receptions for 107 yards and a score as Houston improved to 2-4 on the year.

Stroud's first interception of the season came by way of Travis Hunter as the two-way Jags star became the first player to score a touchdown and record a pick in the same game since Brian Dawkins for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Texans on September 29, 2002.

Trevor Lawrence finished 24 of 41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception as the Jaguars slipped to 4-2 at the end of their fortnight in the UK.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Corgi race entertains Sky Sports presenters Jason Bell and Neil Reynolds at Wembley during the Houston Texans, Jacksonville Jaguars half time show.

Hunter had derailed Houston's attempt to put the game to bed with four minutes left when he intercepted Stroud in the end zone to halt a 12-play drive.

Last week's hero Little delivered again moments later when he converted a 60-yard field goal to tie the game at 31-31 with two minutes to play.

Stroud proceeded to navigate a game-winning drive that included a 19-yard connection to Woody Marks on third-and-two as Houston reached field goal range to set up Fairbairn's defining moment. He delivered on cue.

Having led 17-14 at the break, Houston pushed their lead out to 24-14 on the opening drive of the second half through Noel's 13-yard touchdown catch on third-and-10.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nate Boerkircher stuns the Houston Texans with beautiful one-handed catch in the endzone for the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley.

Jacksonville's reply came courtesy of a one-handed one-yard touchdown grab by tight end Nate Boerkircher to pull within 24-21 after Jakobi Meyers had springboarded the drive with two catches for a combined 50 yards.

Jawhar Jordan, elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's game, scurried clear for a 25-yard touchdown on the ensuing possession as Houston opened up a 10-point cushion.

Back came the Jags, Hunter taming a bullet from Lawrence for a seven-yard touchdown to make it 31-28 after the extra point with 11.26 to play in the fourth quarter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player CJ Stroud's 'perfect' throw connects with Foster Moreau for a one-handed touchdown catch for the Houston Texans against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Houston had struck first in the game when Stroud floated a six-yard touchdown pass to tight end Foster Moreau, rewarding Nico Collins for his 42-yard airborne contested catch in direct coverage from Hunter along the sideline.

The Jags were foiled in their immediate response when Bhayshul Tuten's three-yard touchdown run was nullified by a Brenton Strange holding penalty, before Lawrence was intercepted by Calen Bullock in the end zone while targeting Jakobi Meyers on third-and-goal.

Tuten refused to be denied again when he slalomed through two tackle attempts for a 27-yard touchdown catch-and-run mid-way through the second quarter.

The Jags running back struck again when Lawrence peeled out to his right to float a two-yard strike to Tuten for a 14-10 lead with a minute remaining in the half. Houston responded instantly when Moreau hauled in a one-yard touchdown pass with eight seconds left after Noel's 50-yard reception.
