Sports.title: Poll: Does F1 needs its cost cap – or is it just holding back the smaller teams? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
The difficulty of creating a level playing field for sporting competitions in a world where teams teams are sold for billions has been highlighted by recent developments in the English football Premier League.

Multiple champions Manchester City were found guilty of cheating the league’s Financial Fair Play rules using sham contracts to hide funding of over £830 million . The league is yet to confirm their penalty and the club intends to appeal.

F1 introduced its equivalent rules, the budget cap, five years ago. No teams has committed a breach on anything like the same scale as that seen in the Premier League. When Red Bull was found to have overspent in the first year under the budget cap, but their £1.864m overspend amounts to just 0.2% of Manchester City’s breach. What’s more, Red Bull’s error was not found to be deliberate, unlike Manchester City’s.

Other breaches have occured, including in the recently-introduced engine cost cap. But these have usually been relatively minor procedural matters, nothing on the scale of Manchester City case, which spanned nine seasons.

But while F1’s budget cap appears to have been enforced effectively, is it having a positive effect on the championship?

Some of F1’s smaller teams said they would not have been able to continue without it. However others have expressed concerns the spending limit has created a “cost cap trap”.

Williams team principal James Vowles described the problem recently. “When we did the cost cap, this is way back [during] Covid, when we had a phone call about it, there were three key tasks that we wanted out of it,” he explained.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We wanted long-term financial sustainability, and I think in that goal, not just have we achieved it, but we’ve exceeded it. This business now has good investment that allows us to go on, and they’re businesses. They weren’t businesses before 2021 at all.

“The two others, though, that went with it were sporting equity and, effectively, compression of the field, so effectively competitiveness that compressed together. Those are the three goals of cost cap, and those two have failed.”

Vowles said the data shows the leading four teams are in a strong position under the cost cap. “If I take the last five years of the sport, the five that we’ve been in as cost cap right now, currently the top four teams score 83% of the points. Before that it was in the seventies, just to be clear about it.

“In other words, we have made the situation worse, where the top four are the top four and all the rest of us are fighting over, ballpark, 17% of the points.”

According to Vowles, the chasing teams can’t catch up because the cost cap effectively cements their disadvantage. “When you’re in a cost cap, I’m not spending money on the car. I’m spending millions, tens of millions actually, just on basic systems, so you just know where a part is in the factory. So that’s not going to the car, it’s not going to a front wing, it’s not going to an upgrade. It’s going on systems that I need to do just to do the very basics.

“So, we’re caught in a cost cap trap, because if I do anything short-term – and I always talk about investing in the future, now you understand why – if I do anything that’s about this year, I will slow myself down in the future, and I can’t do that.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have a two-tier championship. That’s not me telling you that. That is just what is on the table right now in terms of points score.”

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem indicated his dissatisfaction with the cost cap last year. “I’m looking at the cost cap and it’s just giving the FIA a headache,” he said. “So what’s the point of it? I don’t see the point.”

Does F1’s cost cap still have a point? Is it protecting the smaller teams from collapse or holding them back from competing with the front runners? And could what happened with Manchester City ever happen in F1?

Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Track Verstappen’s best result Hamilton’s best result Bahrain International Circuit 1st 1st Jeddah Corniche Circuit 1st 1st Albert Park 1st 1st Suzuka 1st 1st Shanghai International Circuit 1st 1st Miami International Autodrome 1st 6th Circuit Gilles Villeneuve 1st 1st Monaco 1st 1st Autodromo do Algarve 2nd 1st Silverstone 1st 1st Red Bull Ring 1st 1st Spa-Francorchamps 1st 1st Hungaroring 1st 1st Monza 1st 1st Madring 2nd DNF Baku City Circuit 1st 1st Istanbul Park 2nd 1st Singapore 1st 1st Circuit of the Americas 1st 1st Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 1st 1st Interlagos 1st 1st Las Vegas Strip Circuit 1st 2nd Losail International Circuit 1st 1st Yas Marina 1st 1st

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

But Alpine’s season has decidedly hit the skids as they failed to score for the third round in a row. It was a particularly frustrating weekend for Pierre Gasly, who finished one place outside the points in both the sprint race and grand prix.

Williams left Singapore point-less, too. Carlos Sainz Jnr got his car into the top 10 early on in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend, but slipped to 14th at the flag.

Sports.title: On This Day: Stroll wins final race before becoming a Formula 1 driver | Brief
Sports.content:
10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

For his last race at Prema, Stroll lined up fourth on the grid behind Joel Eriksson, Jake Hughes and Callum Ilott. Stroll wasn’t the only future F1 driver on the grid: others included Nikita Mazepin (10th), Zhou Guanyu (13th) and George Russell (15th). Anthoine Hubert, who tragically died in a Formula 2 crash in 2019, lined up seventh.

Formula 1 team bosses have said they want to know where the season finale will be held by mid-October.

The series intends to run its final two races as planned in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However ongoing disruption caused by the US-Iran war has put that in doubt and led F1 to enlist the Imola circuit as a potential alternative venue for the final race.

A new report claims F1 could wait until the middle of November before deciding its plans for the final race of the season.

“There were also rumours in Malaysia and Singapore, where the sport has spent the last fortnight, that some sort of deal had been done between Qatar, the UAE and Iran to guarantee security, giving F1 increased confidence to press ahead,” adds the report in The Telegraph.

Sports.title: Official: Camara to make Formula 1 debut with Haas in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara will make his Formula 1 debut for Haas next season.

Haas, one of Ferrari’s customer teams, confirmed the 21-year-old will take the seat vacated by Esteban Ocon at the end of the year. He is expected to partner Oliver Bearman, another member of Ferrari’s driver academy, who has driven for Haas since last year.

Camara has enjoyed a stellar rise through the junior formula series since being picked up by Ferrari in 2022. He currently leads the Formula 2 championship standings, with no indication yet whether the final rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will be able to go ahead.

Like fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto, Camara won the Formula 3 championship at his first attempt. He also won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before.

Camara has already experienced one of Haas’s Formula 1 chassis in a Test of Previous Cars at the Autodromo do Algarve, which will hold the Portuguese Grand Prix next year. He has also tested for Ferrari.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said he is “really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Camara.”

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car,” Komatsu continued, “he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special.”

Camara thanked Komatsu, Haas team owner Gene Haas and the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for his chance to make his F1 debut.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley’s Defeats Overshadow His Finest Boxing Year
Sports.content:
A back-and-forth heavyweight fight captures the public’s collective imagination like few other sporting events. Countless expressions originating or popularized in heavyweight boxing describe competitive sporting events. “A knockdown drag-out contest”, “teams throwing haymakers”, “a slugfest”, “a heavyweight fight”, and many other such phrases regularly feature on football, baseball and basketball broadcasts.

The first fight between Daniel Dubois (24-3, 23 KO) and Fabio Wardley (20-2-1, 19 KO) in May illustrated the fantasy of what many envision in a heavyweight clash. Knockdowns, temerity, mettle, blood, violence. In the end, Daniel Dubois prevailed via technical knockout in the eleventh round. Fabio Wardley lost his championship, but gained the respect of anyone watching. It instantly entered the “fight of the year” conversation and was hailed as a heavyweight classic.

…

This past Saturday, just over five months later, Dubois and Wardley met again. The rematch was anticlimactic by comparison. The fight featured an early knockdown like the first encounter, though this time Daniel Dubois delivered it. Though Wardley tried to resist Dubois’ onslaught, it proved to be futile. Dubois nearly ended the bout inside the first round. But Wardley survived long enough to hear the bell to conclude round one. Ultimately, Wardley’s doggedness just lengthened his suffering.

Sixty seconds later, as round two began, Dubois was patient, waiting to find openings to pound away at Wardley. Dubois did it in short order. In the final minute of round two, Dubois peppered a winded and wounded Wardley with clean, powerful punches. The fight got stopped 2:21 into the second round; it was undoubtedly a fair stoppage. Referee Steve Gray stopped the contest just as Wardley’s trainer Ben Davidson threw in the towel from the corner.

Dubois obliterated Fabio Wardley and extinguished any doubt from fans and media, at least for now.

…

Fabio Wardley was a latecomer to boxing, turning professional at 22 years old with no amateur fights on his resume. Both his age and lack of amateur experience are considered rarities. Four fights into his pro career, Wardley agreed to be managed by Dillian Whyte, a fellow British heavyweight and former sparring partner. Wardley was born in Ipswich, England, and naturally is a lifelong supporter of Ipswich Town Football Club. He attained a dream by fighting at Ipswich Town’s stadium, Portman Road, in June 2025. His knockout win there over Justis Huni helped propel Wardley to recognition as 2025’s British Boxer of the Year, according to multiple outlets. An upset victory over former world champion Joseph Parker earned Wardley the WBO’s interim heavyweight championship. Wardley’s banner year of 2025 set him up to challenge Daniel Dubois in May for the vacant WBO heavyweight title.

…

On Saturday, Fabio Wardley was walloped. This year, Wardley has zero wins and two losses, both by technical knockout. But boxing fans will always remember the slugfest Wardley and Dubois had in May. While 2025 was Wardley’s most successful year in boxing, he will inevitably be associated with Daniel Dubois and their classic fight five months ago. In a career in which he has beaten former world champions and scored devastating knockouts, boxing fans will most fondly remember Fabio Wardley for a fight he lost.

It might not be fair, but it is reality. In a way, it is endearing, though. Even if Fabio Wardley never competes for a heavyweight championship again, the Ipswichian has forever earned a place in heavyweight boxing lore for his performance on May 9, 2026.

…

Sports and society at large are infatuated with analytics and data. Decades from now, when a young boxing fan asks their personalized robot about Fabio Wardley, they will be unimpressed by consecutive knockout losses. But if that young fan finds an old head and mentions Fabio Wardley, they will hear about his toughness, how he could have won a title in a different era, who Wardley reminds them of, and whatever else. Wardley and Dubois have earned remembrance in highlight reels and recollections, the greatest accolade of all.

Sports.title: Dalton Smith Wants Shakur Stevenson After Alberto Puello
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith is already eyeing a massive unification bout with Shakur Stevenson, even with his first WBC light welterweight title defense against Alberto Puello just days away.

Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) meets Puello on October 24 at Utilita Arena Sheffield. The unbeaten titleholder wants this victory to catapult him toward marquee names. Shakur sits near the top of his target list, but Puello can ruin everything.

“I’m boxing to be a part of the biggest fights possible. Of course the Shakur fight would be up there as one of the biggest. I’d love to be a part of that,” Smith told the Boxing World YouTube channel. “But of course, I have to get through Puello first.”

Smith grabbed the WBC belt back in January by stopping Subriel Matias inside five rounds during his US debut. Blowing through Matias earned him huge momentum, though it guarantees nothing against Puello.

Puello brings an awkward southpaw style. Smith will not get the same gifts he received from Matias, who walked straight in until he got caught by heavy counters. Puello is far more than a tune-up on the way to a Shakur payday. This matchup tests whether Dalton can defend his crown against a completely different kind of opponent.

“I don’t overlook what’s in front of me, but once I get the job done against Puello, I want to be chasing the biggest fights possible,” Smith said.

Puello (25-1, 11 KOs) has his own motives to spoil the party and steal that massive future date for himself. Calling out Shakur is the easy part for Smith. He still has to leave the ring with the belt.

Even if he gets past Puello, Dalton is overlooking the obstacles that will prevent him from fighting Shakur next. The network and promotional divide makes the Shakur-Smith fight virtually impossible to assemble right now. Shakur is signed with Zuffa and locked into Paramount+, while Smith is a Matchroom flagship fighter tied to DAZN.

Dual-network broadcasts only happen when the revenue numbers are astronomical, like Gervonta Davis against Ryan Garcia or massive undisputed heavyweight cards funded by deep foreign pockets. Dalton Smith versus Shakur Stevenson is nowhere near that category.

Neither guy moves US pay-per-view buys on that scale, and Zuffa has zero incentive to share production, split domestic rights, or loan out Shakur to DAZN for an ordinary regular-subscription card.

Dalton is known almost exclusively in the UK, and Shakur has struggled to build an audience that translates into commercial event revenue.

Zuffa Boxing did not bring Shakur to Paramount+ just to farm him out to DAZN or hand Matchroom control of an international production. If Zuffa wants Shakur in a unification or a meaningful fight at 140 pounds, they have zero business justification to share the pie with an outside streaming rival on an event with minimal domestic pay-per-view appetite.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford, Tim Bradley Challenge Fundora Stoppage
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora’s last-second stoppage of Ermal Hadribeaj drew objections during a post-fight discussion involving Terence Crawford and Tim Bradley, while Dan Rafael called for the result to be changed to a decision.

Hadribeaj appeared able to continue when the referee halted Saturday’s fight in Las Vegas. The unusual ending put a cloud over Fundora’s WBC junior middleweight title defense, with the dispute focused on Hadribeaj beating the count after the final bell had already sounded.

“All he had to do was get on his feet,” came one objection during the discussion involving Crawford, Bradley and the referee.

The referee defended his intervention by pointing to Hadribeaj falling back into the ropes and arguing that another attack would have left him in trouble.

“If there’s five seconds left, that guy gets destroyed,” he said.

But those five seconds did not exist. That is the problem with using a possible follow-up attack to justify the stoppage. Hadribeaj had no more fighting left to do if he had beaten the count after the final bell.

Rafael made that argument forcefully on X, urging Hadribeaj’s team to protest to the Nevada State Athletic Commission.

“HE BEAT THE COUNT and the bell had already rung,” Rafael said. “Won’t be surprised at all if the NSAC changes the result to a unanimous decision.”

That was Rafael’s expectation, rather than an announced commission action. Still, his criticism gives Hadribeaj’s team a specific issue to raise: whether the referee improperly extended the process beyond the completed count when the fight had already ended.

This is about dollars and cents, not just hurt feelings. Getting tagged with an illegitimate knockout loss hurts Hadribeaj’s marketability and ruins his leverage for future paydays. Fundora keeps his win on the cards anyway, but the commission needs to step in, overturn the bogus stoppage, and take an undeserved KO loss off Hadribeaj’s record.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Tells Moses Itauma: “No Time For Crying”
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic is having a grand time talking down to Moses Itauma. As the young heavyweight mopes over his first defeat and fixates on replays, Hrgovic delivered a blunt reality check: stop crying, get back in the gym, and figure out how to win when your opponent refuses to fall over.

Itauma admitted this week that rewatching the bout eats away at him. He landed his best artillery, watched Hrgovic walk straight through it, and kept winging power shots until his gas tank emptied completely. He sounds like a fighter in denial, still convinced the knockout was right there if he had just thrown a little harder.

Hrgovic responded with dripping condescension, offering to comfort the 21-year-old prospect like a disappointed toddler.

“I’ll tell him, ‘Look, Moses, everything will be good,'” Hrgovic told The Stomping Ground. “I will cuddle him … on the head, like, ‘Moses, everything will be good. Don’t be upset.'”

The mocking humor carried an unforgiving point. Hrgovic pointed out that a loss should light a fire under a fighter rather than shatter his nerve, before making sure to remind everyone who dismantled the hype train.

“You must learn from that that you can’t knock out Filip Hrgovic,” he said. “You must learn you can’t knock out everyone. You must be ready for a 12-round fight.”

That diagnosis is right on the money. Itauma got exposed by his own reliance on early blowouts. Once his power failed to create a shortcut, he had no Plan B, frantically emptying his reserves against an immovable target walking him down.

Surviving at the top level means knowing how to bank rounds without punching yourself into exhaustion. Itauma needs to accept that durable heavyweights will absorb his Sunday punch and keep coming.

Hrgovic threw in obligatory compliments about Itauma’s raw speed, but the core message was pure dismissal.

“No time for crying. Go back to the gym, and that’s it, man. Simple.”

Staring at the tape will not undo the beating. Itauma either learns how to box when the stoppage vanishes, or the next seasoned heavyweight will run the exact same script on him.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley II – FIGHT REVIEW
Sports.content:
This past Saturday on the 17th of October, from The O2 Arena in London, England, in a championship rematch that was available live worldwide on DAZN PPV – reigning WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois made an emphatic statement, stopping former titleholder Fabio Wardley in the 2nd round to successfully retain his championship.

Get DAZN Ultimate Tier HERE

The heavyweight division has been in total chaos ever since Oleksandr Usyk vacated his collection of alphabet belts, leaving the rest of the division battling for supremacy in a wide-open landscape. Entering the night, the big question was whether Wardley could make the necessary pacing adjustments after dropping Dubois twice early before being stopped in the 11th round of their first encounter five months ago. Instead, Dubois erased all doubt immediately and authored a destructive blowout.

Rather than another back-and-forth war of attrition, Dubois completely flipped the script from their first clash right out of the gate. In the opening seconds of round 1, Dubois caught Wardley flush with a booming shot that dropped the challenger hard to the canvas. Wardley beat the count, but he remained on unsteady legs for the rest of the frame. Staying cool, calm, and composed, Dubois patiently picked his spots and battered Wardley mercilessly before the bell.

Wardley came out for the 2nd round trying to establish his footing and survive the storm, but Dubois was completely dialed in. Stalking his hurt rival with authority, Dubois unleashed another heavy barrage of clubbing shots traps along the ropes, prompting Wardley’s corner to mercifully throw in the towel to save their fighter from further punishment.

This edition of Rummy’s Corner provides a full recap and post-fight review of Dubois’s dominant title defense, while exploring what could be next in the heavyweight division. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: “The Towering Inferno” Fundora Stops Hadribeaj in Final Round
Sports.content:
WBC super welterweight champion Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora stopped Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the twelfth and final round of an action-packed but often sloppy fight at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas, Nevada.

Promoters Tom Brown of TGB Promotions and Sampson Lewkowicz of Sampson Boxing presented the card Saturday on DAZN and TNT.

In the main event, southpaw Fundora, 25-1-1 (17 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped fellow southpaw Hadribeaj, 23-1-1 (8 KOs), of Tirana, Albania, and Miami Beach, Florida, at 2:59 of the final round.

In the second round, Fundora used his considerable height advantage to hurt Hadribeaj early. The challenger fought back and had Fundora in trouble near the end of the round. In the third, referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point from Hadribeaj for excessive holding.

There was nonstop action from the fourth through the tenth as Hadribeaj forced his way inside and Fundora answered with short punches. The challenger made it competitive, although Fundora held an overall edge and increasingly found success with his body attack.

In the eleventh round, Taylor deducted another point from Hadribeaj for holding. Despite his height disadvantage, the challenger continued trying to force the fight at close range.

In the closing seconds of the twelfth, Fundora dropped Hadribeaj with a left hand. Hadribeaj beat the count but was in no condition to continue, prompting Taylor to wave it off with one second remaining.

In the co-main event, former WBA super middleweight champion Armando “Toro” Resendiz, 17-3 (11 KOs), of Guayabitos, Mexico, defeated Koen Mazoudier, 16-5-1 (6 KOs), of Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia, by unanimous decision over ten action-packed rounds.

Resendiz rocked Mazoudier with a right hand to the chin in the final seconds of the fourth round, knocking him off balance. From the sixth through the ninth, Mazoudier pressed the action and fought his way back into the contest, giving the crowd plenty to cheer about while Resendiz continued landing the heavier punches.

In the final minute of the tenth, Resendiz hurt Mazoudier with a flurry of unanswered shots. The Australian survived to hear the final bell.

The scores were 98-92 and 97-93 twice. Harvey Dock was the referee.

In an eight-round super middleweight bout, Jaime Osuna, 12-0 (5 KOs), of Guerrero Negro, Baja California Sur, Mexico, won a majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi, 13-1-1 (5 KOs), of Palermo, Italy, and Brooklyn, New York.

Osuna suffered a cut over his right eye from a left hook in the third round, which Cangelosi took with his cleaner work.

In the fifth, Osuna rocked Cangelosi early as the fight developed into a slugfest. Cangelosi answered in the seventh, catching Osuna with a right hand to the chin in the closing seconds.

Both had their moments in the eighth and final round, fighting hard with the result still in doubt.

Two judges scored it 77-75 for Osuna, while the third had it even at 76-76. Robert Hoyle was the referee.

Super middleweight Marco “El Tiburon” Romero, 16-0 (14 KOs), of Olathe, Kansas, stopped Matias Ferreira, 8-4 (3 KOs), of Rosario, Uruguay, at 1:54 of the first round of their scheduled eight-round bout.

Ferreira landed a left hook midway through the opening round, but Romero countered with a right hand to the chin that dropped him onto the seat of his trunks. Referee Tony Weeks stopped the contest following the knockdown.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

The scheduled bout between Brandon Figueroa and Tomoki Kameda was canceled after Figueroa became ill following his weight cut. Figueroa was also stripped of his WBA featherweight title after failing to make the division limit.

Sports.title: Ennis vs. Kelly Winner Targeted By Sebastian Fundora
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the Jaron Ennis–Josh Kelly winner next, but a potential Ennis fight comes with a financial obstacle: promoter Sampson Lewkowicz’s demand for a 50-50 purse split.

Fundora called for undisputed after stopping Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round. The WBC junior middleweight champion sounded ready to pursue the other belts, although agreeing on an opponent is only part of getting a unification made.

“Absolutely, let’s go for undisputed,” Fundora told DAZN when asked about facing the Ennis–Kelly winner. “We will break them down like we broke this guy, like the guy before that, before that, and before. We’ll keep breaking these guys down.”

Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) had just completed his fourth successful title defense, wearing down Hadribeaj with short punches and sustained body work before dropping him with a left hand at 2:59 of the final round.

That performance supported his description of breaking opponents down. Hadribeaj made the early rounds competitive by crowding Fundora, but the champion gradually took over through his greater activity inside.

Getting Ennis into the ring could require a different kind of patience. Lewkowicz has called for an equal split for Fundora against Ennis, leaving the financial terms as something the camps would have to resolve if Ennis beats Kelly.

There is no agreement established by Fundora’s post-fight comments, nor do they show that Ennis has accepted or rejected those terms. The potential obstacle is whether an equal split becomes a firm condition or a starting position in negotiations.

Fundora has made his preference clear. If Ennis wins, the next question will be whether the promoters can find a price both sides accept and turn that undisputed ambition into a scheduled fight.

Tonight’s showing only hurts Fundora’s negotiating position. Needing until the final second of the twelfth round to finish a gritty but limited challenger like Hadribeaj showed the exact vulnerabilities that have always followed Fundora. He surrenders his 6’6″ frame, stays glued in the pocket, eats clean shots on the inside, and relies strictly on outlasting foes in a war of attrition.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Stops Ermal Hadribeaj With One Second Left
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora stopped Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round, finishing a physically taxing fight with a left hand after gradually wearing down the challenger with body punches and a higher work rate.

The victory gave Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) his fourth successful defense of the WBC junior middleweight title on Saturday night at The Chelsea at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs) suffered his first defeat after making the champion work considerably harder than his heavy favorite status suggested.

Hadribeaj had little interest in remaining at the end of Fundora’s punches. The challenger stayed low, moved inside and landed hard shots, forcing the taller champion into a fight where his height and reach offered fewer benefits.

A long left hand buzzed Hadribeaj in the second round, but he recovered quickly and returned to pressing the action. Referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point for holding in the third, adding an early cost to the challenger’s attempts to crowd and smother Fundora.

The inside fighting remained competitive through the middle rounds. Hadribeaj landed some of the heavier individual punches, while Fundora answered with more frequent short shots and uppercuts.

Fundora’s body attack became increasingly effective as the fight progressed. Rather than consistently creating distance, he found room to punch where Hadribeaj wanted to fight, digging downstairs and keeping his hands moving.

That made the challenger’s approach harder to sustain. Getting close no longer prevented Fundora from scoring, and Hadribeaj increasingly held as the champion continued working.

Taylor took another point from Hadribeaj in the 11th. By then, Fundora was producing the cleaner, more consistent offense, leaving the challenger needing a dramatic finish.

The decisive punch came from the champion instead. Fundora maintained his pressure in the final round before a left hand dropped Hadribeaj and ended the fight at 2:59.

Ghana News.title: NPP demands publication of invoices for GH¢27m South Africa evacuation flights
Ghana News.content:
The Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has challenged Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to publish the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices for three chartered flights used to evacuate Ghanaians from South Africa.

He says the documents are needed to establish the actual cost of the flights following claims that the government paid $750,000 for each aircraft.

Speaking at a press briefing on Sunday, October 18, Miracles Aboagye said documents released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, including its response to a Right to Information (RTI) request dated September 18, 2026, and a report to Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee, raised questions about the expenditure.

He said the documents showed that GH¢27,183,700 was spent on chartered flights, representing 55 per cent of the total evacuation cost, but did not include invoices, contracts or the names of the operators.

Mr Aboagye further claimed that information available to the NPP indicated that the first three chartered flights were operated by Ethiopian Airlines and arranged through a person identified as Mr Vanderpuye.

He alleged that each flight may have been billed at nearly $300,000 above its actual cost, insisting that the original invoices would help clarify the discrepancy.

According to him, the Minister's documents put the cost of each flight at "$750,000, while the party's industry checks suggested that chartering a flight through Ethiopian Airlines or Air Tanzania should cost between $180,000 and $300,000."

The three flights, he said reportedly transported about 900 passengers from South Africa to Ghana.

“We put this to the Minister directly, and we invite him to prove it wrong with paper, not words. Publish the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices for all three flights, so we can have some proper conversation with the airline as to how and why it ripped off the country at such a crucial time,” he said.

Mr Aboagye also questioned the Ministry's relationship with Mr Vanderpuye, who he alleged arranged the flights.

He asked whether the Ministry's Chief Director had requested fresh invoices from Mr Vanderpuye in September and, if so, why invoices for flights completed months earlier needed to be reissued.

He further demanded the release of detailed records from Ghana's High Commission in Pretoria covering the flights, payments and assistance provided to the evacuees.

Mr Aboagye also called on Mr Ablakwa to "clarify allegations that his bodyguard had received $10,000 from the evacuation arrangements."

He asked the Minister to confirm whether the officer had been dismissed and explain the purpose of the alleged payment and the circumstances surrounding the reported dismissal.

“If the figures are honest, the original invoices will settle this in a day. If they are not produced, Ghanaians will draw their own conclusions,” he said.

The allegations of overbilling and the alleged payment to the bodyguard were not independently established in the statement. The Foreign Affairs Minister's response to the specific claims was not included in the material provided.

Ghana News.title: NPP gives Ablakwa 7-day ultimatum over South Africa evacuation spending, vows further action
Ghana News.content:
Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister of Foreign Affairs

The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has given Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa seven days to produce documents covering the expenditure on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa, warning of further action if its demands are not met.

Speaking at a press briefing on Sunday, October 18, the Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, said the party is demanding the release of charter flight invoices and contracts, payment vouchers, signed payment records and a complete list of the 1,964 evacuees with proof of payment against each name.

"Produce the complete set of documents within 7 days. Lay before the RTI requisition and Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee every charter invoice and contract, every payment voucher, every signed sheet, and the full list of 1,964 evacuees with proof of payment against each name," he said.

He also indicated that the party is seeking details of the selection of the charter operator under the Public Procurement Act and an explanation of the GH¢16 million reportedly involved in the evacuation arrangements, including whether the amount was paid in cash or used for purchases.

The NPP further wants the Minister to clarify discrepancies in two sets of figures relating to "ASKY Airlines and different versions of a letter identified as CC/7, including which version was submitted to the Auditor-General."

As part of its demands, the party is calling for an independent audit by an internationally recognised firm, with the terms of reference and findings made public.

Mr Aboagye noted that the Auditor-General's review of the expenditure was welcome but should not be the only measure of accountability.

The NPP warned that failure to meet the demands would prompt it to support the Minority in Parliament to pursue the matter, including through urgent questions to the Minister.

It also intends to "formally petition the Auditor-General to prioritise the evacuation expenditure in the special audit and pursue further remedies under the Right to Information Act."

The party said it would continue raising questions about the expenditure until the relevant documents and explanations were made available.

The NPP further questioned Mr Ablakwa's commitment to accountability, arguing that he had previously pressed successive governments for detailed explanations of public expenditure while in opposition.

It said the same standard of transparency should apply to the current administration.

“The 1,964 Ghanaians who fled South Africa suffered enough. They should not now become a headline figure behind which public money cannot be traced,” the party said.

The NPP maintained that the release of the documents was necessary to establish how public funds were spent and restore public confidence in the evacuation arrangements.

The demands follow concerns raised by the party over the reported cost of chartered flights and the supporting documentation for the evacuation expenditure.

Ghana News.title: Man in police custody for alleged murder of a 2-year-old in Hohoe

Man in police custody for alleged murder of a 2-year-old in Hohoe

26-year-old Robert Akator has been apprehended by the Volta North Regional Police Command for the alleged murder of a two-year-old boy at Wli-Afegame, in the Hohoe Municipality.

He added that the suspect is in “police custody assisting with the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident.

conduct their work professionally.

“Members of the public are also encouraged to provide credible information to the Police to support the investigation and enhance public safety.”

“The Volta North Regional Police Command remains committed to protecting lives, maintaining

law and order, and ensuring public safety”, he concluded.

Ghana News.title: Over half of South Africa evacuation expenditure lacks invoices – NPP
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says more than half of the money spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa is not supported by invoices in documents released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Speaking at a press briefing on Sunday, October 18, the Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, said GH¢27.18 million was spent on chartered flights, representing about 55 per cent of the total evacuation expenditure, without invoices or contracts provided in the documents cited by the party.

He said the Ministry's response to a Right to Information (RTI) request dated September 18, 2026, and its report to Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee did not contain invoices, contracts or the names of the flight operators.

"More than half the money comes with no invoice. GHS 27,183,700 was spent on chartered flights. That is 55 per cent of the entire cost. Not one invoice. Not one contract. Not even the name of the operator. Only a sentence saying the flights were arranged. Emergency explains the urgency. It does not excuse the missing receipts," he said.

Mr Aboagye questioned why the Ministry had not provided the supporting documents for the charter flights.

He also questioned the reported cost of $750,000 for each of three chartered flights, alleging that the amount was significantly higher than the $180,000 to $300,000 he said industry checks suggested was the expected cost of chartering a flight through Ethiopian Airlines or Air Tanzania.

The NPP further called for the publication of the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices to establish the actual cost of the flights and address its concerns about possible overbilling.

"Information reaching the New Patriotic Party indicates that the first three charter flights were operated by Ethiopian Airlines and arranged through a Mr Vanderpuye. We are further informed that each of those three flights may have been billed at close to USD 300,000 above its true cost. According to the Minister’s own documents, each charter flights cost $750,000. We had 3 chartered flights to lift about 900 passengers. That means, it costs the state $2,500 to buy a seat for a single passenger travelling from South Africa to Ghana.

"Our checks from the industry place the maximum cost of chartering a flight from Ethiopian Airlines and Air Tanzania should cost between $180,000 and $300,000 for one. Strangely, the Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs is telling us he paid $750,000 for one airplane. Just one.

"We put this to the Minister directly, and we invite him to prove it wrong with paper, not words. Publish the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices for all three flights, so we can have some proper conversation with the airline as to how and why it ripped off the country at such a crucial time. Tell Ghanaians why his Ministry has fallen out with the very man who arranged them."

Ghana News.title: 2026/27: Medeama suffer first defeat as Aduana, Kotoko return to winning ways
Ghana News.content:
Medeama SC suffered their first defeat of the Premier League season, while Aduana FC and Asante Kotoko returned to winning ways in an eventful Matchday 7 weekend of the Ghana Premier League.

Dreams FC snatched a dramatic stoppage-time point on the road, and Debibi United climbed out of the relegation zone after securing a crucial home victory.

FC Samartex 1996 secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Medeama at the Nsenkyire Arena, a, with Christian Agyenim scoring three minutes into injury time after Joshuah Fuseini had opened the scoring in the 54th minute.

Dominic Amponsah briefly restored parity for the defending champions in the 79th minute, but Agyenim’s late winner handed Samartex all three points.

Despite the setback, Medeama remain top of the table with 14 points, level with Hearts of Oak and Samartex after seven matches.

Asante Kotoko also returned to winning ways with a 2-1 victory over Young Apostles at the Baba Yara Stadium. Hubert Gyau opened the scoring in the 70th minute before Solomon Nsor Asaah doubled the lead 12 minutes later.

Huziaf Iddrisu pulled one back for Young Apostles with a late direct free-kick, but Kotoko held on to claim a valuable victory and climb to sixth place. Young Apostles, meanwhile, remain in the relegation zone.

Aduana FC bounced back from their previous defeat with a narrow 1-0 win over FC AshantiGold 04 at the Nana Agyeman Badu I Park. Abubakar Adams reacted quickest to a rebound from Seidu Saana’s free-kick to score the decisive goal in the 40th minute.

AshantiGold’s hopes of finding an equaliser suffered another blow when Akwasi Afari was sent off, allowing the Fire Boys to secure all three points.

Dreams FC produced one of the weekend’s late dramas, scoring in stoppage time to earn a 1-1 draw against Port City at the Daasebre Boamah Darko II Park.

Samuel Aryee Baadu gave the hosts the lead shortly after the restart with a powerful strike, but Kelvin Ahiable struck late to deny Port City victory.

Dreams remain bottom of the standings but will take encouragement from the hard-earned point.

Swedru All Blacks continued their impressive home form with a convincing 2-0 victory over Karela United. Eric Wiafe Darkwah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the ninth minute before setting up Faisal Charwetey for the second in the 59th minute.

The result secured consecutive league wins for the Black Magicians, while Karela remain in search of their first away point of the campaign.

Basake Holy Stars maintained their perfect home record with a 1-0 victory over Bechem United at the AAK II Park. Bismark Teye Tetteh scored the decisive goal early in the second half as Holy Stars returned to winning ways and climbed to fifth place.

The defeat also extended Bechem United’s winless run against Holy Stars in the Premier League to five matches.

Debibi United climbed out of the relegation zone after edging Bibiani Gold Stars 1-0 at the Debibi Presby Park.

Maxwell Agyemang’s strike just before half-time proved decisive, ending the hosts’ three-match winless run and moving them level on seven points with Gold Stars.

The victory provided a timely boost for the league newcomers, while Gold Stars missed the opportunity to build on their previous weekend’s win.

With seven matches played, the league table remains tightly contested at the top, with Medeama, Hearts of Oak and Samartex all on 14 points.

Ghana News.title: Economy still in low-risk credit environment, credit-to-GDP gap remains negative – BoG
Ghana News.content:
Dr Johnson Asiama, BoG Governor

The credit-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP) gap remained negative in the first eight months of 2026, indicating the economy is still in a low-risk credit environment.

According to the Bank of Ghana, though there has been continuous growth in credit, the growth is weaker relative to the growth in the size of the economy.

“The negative gap points to the absence of excessive credit build-up and limited systemic risks and signals room for measured credit expansion to further support the real sector of the economy”, the Bank of Ghana revealed in its October 2026 Banking Sector Development Report.

According to the Central Bank, the recovery in credit growth has been underpinned by the resilience of the banking sector, which continues to facilitate financial intermediation.

It added that the favourable macroeconomic conditions is expected to continue to sustain the recovery in private sector credit without creating stress on overall financial stability.

Macro-financial Risk Assessment Map

Meanwhile, macro-financial risk assessment showed a projected moderation in risks as at end-September 2026 compared to the same period last year.

Risks from the global macroeconomic environment eased on the back of lower inflation and easing lending conditions in advanced economies.

On the domestic front, risks moderated, reflecting the impact of a declining fiscal deficit, lower inflation and exchange rate stability as well as declining public debt.

The risks from the corporate and household sectors declined, supported by enhanced debt-servicing capacity of both the corporate and household sectors.

In the outlook, risks are expected to generally remain unchanged, however, the risk profile could shift depending on the geopolitical developments in the Middle East.

“Such global developments have implications for the domestic economy and the corporate and household sectors. That notwithstanding, the near-term outlook for the domestic economy remains favourable considering the expected low levels of inflation, strong reserve build-up and improved financing conditions”, the Bank of Ghana concluded.

Ghana News.title: Banks’ profitability moderates, but record GH¢9.2bn profit in 8 months of 2026
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Johnson Asiama

The banking industry remained profitable at the end of August 2026, although profitability moderated compared with the corresponding period in 2025.

Profit-after-tax (PAT) declined marginally to GH¢9.2 billion from GH¢9.7 billion a year earlier. This represented a contraction of 5.7%, compared with growth of 46.1% recorded in August 2025.

Similarly, profit-before-tax (PBT) contracted by 5.7% on a year-on-year basis, in contrast to the 42.0% growth recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

According to the October 2026 Banking Sector Development Report, growth across the banking industry's major income lines moderated during the review period, except for fees and commissions income, which increased by 17.9% in August 2026. This is compared with 13.1% a year earlier.

In contrast, net interest income contracted by 4.2%, reversing the 21.8% growth recorded in August 2025, largely reflecting the low-interest-rate environment and its dampening effect on interest earnings.

Similarly, the growth in other income slowed relative to the corresponding period in 2025.

The growth in the banking industry's cost base moderated during the review period, with operating expenses increasing by 6.4% in August 2026, down from 19.5% a year earlier.

The moderation reflected slower growth in staff costs and a contraction in non-staff expenses. In contrast, provisions for depreciation, bad debts and impairment losses rose sharply by 76.3%, reversing the 46.0% contraction recorded in August 2025.

Return on Assets and Return on Equity

The profitability indicators for the banking sector moderated in August 2026, reflecting the slowdown in earnings growth during the review period.

The industry’s Return on Equity (ROE) declined to 22.2% in August 2026 from 32.2% in August 2025. Similarly, Return on Assets (ROA) decreased to 4.3% from 5.6% over the same period.

Interest Margin and Spread

Interest spread for the industry narrowed to 5.9% in August 2026 from 7.9% in August 2025.

The decrease in spread resulted from the marginal decline in interest payable to 2.2%, from 3.8% a year earlier.

Gross yields also declined to 8.1% in August 2026 compared to 11.6% a year ago.

The ratio of gross income to total assets (asset utilisation) also dropped to 7.3% from 9.2%, whereas the profitability ratio also recorded a marginal decline to 25.3% in August 2026 from 25.4% in August 2025.

Ghana News.title: IMF/ World Bank signs agreement with UAE over holding 2029 Annual Meetings in Abu Dhabi
Ghana News.content:
The World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have signed an agreement with the United Arab Emirates to hold the 2029 Annual Meetings in Abu Dhabi.

The President of the World Bank Group, Ajay Banga and the Managing Director of the IMF, Kristalina Georgieva, initialled the agreement on behalf of their respective Institutions, while Mohamed bin Hadi Al Hussaini, Minister of State for Financial Affairs, UAE and Khaled Mohamed Balama, Governor of the Central Bank, UAE, signed for the UAE.

Speaking at the signing Programme in Bangkok, Thailand, on the Sidelines of the Annual IMF/World Bank meetings, Ajay Banga expressed his excitement about the UAE hosting the 2029 Annual Meetings.

He stated that “we are very delighted that the UAE, Abu Dhabi is the destination of the next Annual Meetings”.

Mr. Banga also highlighted how significant UAE is hosting this Annual Meetings in 2029 is to the group that also happens to host the World Bank’s Knowledge Hub on Gender.

“The World Group is really delighted, because I have had an opportunity of attending two meetings outside Washington, DC, USA, and that has been excellent”, the World Bank President stated.

On her Part,Kristalina Georgieva said, “We are all coming to Abu Dhabi, so prepare for the world. Indeed, the UAE is changing rapidly, a country that is transforming every day”.

“These Annual Meetings outside Washington, DC are the most memorable ones for participants and even the IMF/ World Bank”, the Managing Director of the IMF stated.

Madam Georgieva reminded officials of the UAE that “ We spent a week here in Bangkok, and you saw the preparation, the food and culture, so I can say that Thailand has set a very high standard”.

“But I am optimistic that the UAE is always able to meet this challenge”, she added.

The Minister of State for Financial Affairs, UAE, said the UAE appreciates the opportunity and would build on the partnership that exit with the IMF/ World Bank.

He said, “we look forward to welcoming members of the IMF/ World Bank back to the UAE after 26 years”.

“I will like to thank the World Bank and the IMF for the trust in our country”, the Minister of State for Financial Affairs, UAE, added.

The Governor of the Central Bank, UAE, for his part said the hosting of the Annual Meetings in 2029 is a vote of confidence in the economy of UAE as well as “our business model and hope to see all the members of IMF/ World Bank in our country soon.

UAE Hosting the Annual Meetings in 2029

The Board of Governors of the IMF/ World Bank in April 2026 voted to select Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates as the host country for the October 2029 meetings.

According to the Finance Ministry of the UAE, hosting the meeting is in line with the UAE's ​strategic vision of strengthening international partnerships.

The last time the Annual Meetings were held in the UAE was in 2003 in Dubai.

The Annual Meetings are usually held for two consecutive years at the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund headquarters in Washington, D.C. and every third year in one of the institutions’ member countries.

The 2026 Annual Meetings, which were hosted in Bangkok, Thailand, from October 12 to 18, have received a lot of praise from the Managing Director of the IMF.

The Meetings bring together central bankers, ministers of finance and development, private sector leaders, and a wide range of stakeholders across civil society, media, and academia to discuss the most pressing issues facing the global economy. This includes global economic and financial stability, job creation, and poverty eradication.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: ‘Anger and shame’: Macron denounces France’s nationwide rioting, looting
World.content:
President Macron promises to increase security, but stops short of announcing a state of emergency or curfew.

French President Emmanuel Macron has expressed “anger and shame” over what he described as violent protesters’ attempts “to bring down the republic”.

In a televised address to the nation on Sunday, Macron promised that rioters and looters would “pay for their crimes”, after Saturday saw some of the worst urban violence in France in years.

The country’s Interior Ministry said that nearly 2,400 people were arrested on Saturday, with about 1,000 police and gendarmes injured.

Macron said there must be a distinction between protesters with “legitimate demands” and “those who destroyed, smashed, and looted”.

The president pledged to launch a “crisis unit” to provide “urgent aid … for those who are going through difficult moments”. He added that “lessons will be learned” after the destructive violence erupted this weekend.

“We need to be clear: yesterday, our law enforcement officers and officials, despite their professionalism, were subjected to unprecedented violence in several cities,” he said.

“I’ve asked the government to provide all the lessons learned and to be able to anticipate it to make sure that this does not happen again,” Macron said, adding: “We need unity, we need calm and respect.”

Reporting from Paris, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler said Macron’s speech had “perhaps no surprises”.

“Whether it’s going to be enough to placate some people, I’m not really sure, because those who have been out protesting say they’re fed up of hearing these sorts of speeches by the French president,” Butler said.



The protests are quickly becoming a political football for parties vying for public support ahead of presidential elections next year.

Left-wing presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said the French government is “solely responsible” for the destruction during protests, and has “failed to organise the maintenance of public order”.

Far-right presidential hopeful Jordan Bardella called Macron’s Sunday speech “lamentable” and “cowardly”, saying the government has nothing left to offer the French people and “cannot even protect them”.
