World.title: India’s crackdown on cockroaches, critics and cameras
World.content:
A government at war with its critics – from young protesters to the media.

A wave of youth-led protests has returned to the streets of India’s capital, Delhi, after media reports revealed that the Electoral Commission removed about 130 million names from voter lists.

These protests differ from the unrest that exploded in July, though, by the attacks on the media.

Dozens of journalists and content creators have been detained, assaulted or blocked from doing their jobs. But tightening the screws on critical reporting doesn’t appear to be working, as a new generation rises to challenge the government.

Contributors:

Saba Naqvi – Author and journalist

Smita Sharma – Multimedia journalist

Shyam Meera Singh – Founder, Strike Originals

Sushant Singh – Lecturer, Yale University

On our radar

Pakistan has declared a state of emergency in the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, following protests calling for the release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan.

The state’s response has followed a familiar pattern: A media blackout and internet shutdown, while casting protesters as rebels.

Reporter: Tariq Nafi

The rise of digital micro-Bolsonaros

It’s been more than three years since Jair Bolsonaro fell from power, yet the right-wing movement he started is still without a clear leader. Into that gap has stepped a new crop of young evangelical political influencers, who are tapping into a decades-old religious media machine to build their audience.

Their viral content ricochets across social feeds, mobilising followers and voters in ways old-school politicians just can’t match.

The Listening Post’s Nicholas Muirhead reports on Brazil’s evangelical influencers and the political space they are looking to take over.

Featuring:

Anna Virginia Balloussier – Journalist, Folha De Sao Paulo

Caro Evangelista – Executive director, Iser

Magali Cunha – Editor-in-chief, Berreia Project

World.title: How will Europe deal with youth-led protests?
World.content:
Demonstrations are spreading across the continent.

Weeks of student protests in France have grown into some of the worst unrest in Europe in recent years.

The demonstrations started as a call for reforms to the education system. But they have since expanded into protests against the high cost of living and planned cuts to social services.

And France is not alone. Demonstrators have taken to the streets in other parts of Europe. They are venting their frustrations against leaders they say have failed to address their needs, and putting pressure on their governments.

And right-wing parties are looking to seize the moment to make political gains.

Presenter:

James Bays

Guests:

Diane De Vignemont – Independent journalist and historian

Julius Fintelmann – Co-founder and editor-in-chief at The European Correspondent

Jaime Velazquez – Independent journalist who specialises in the political landscape in Spain

World.title: Clarence Seedorf calls out genocide in first Corinthians press conference
World.content:
Clarence Seedorf calls out genocide in first Corinthians press conference

NewsFeed Clarence Seedorf calls out genocide in first Corinthians press conference

In his first press conference as the newly appointed coach of Brazil’s Corinthians, Clarence Seedorf says football must be kept in perspective while genocides and conflicts continue around the world.

World.title: Russia’s war on Ukraine ‘must be brought to an end’, Zelenskyy says
World.content:
Ukraine’s president says communication between Washington and Kyiv ‘virtually nonstop’, despite a spat with Trump.

Share Russia’s war on Ukraine ‘must be brought to an end’, Zelenskyy says on social media

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that the war with Russia “must be brought to an end” and that his country is preparing for the “next steps” of diplomacy to end the conflict.

Zelenskyy said on X on Sunday that he had a “conversation with the American president’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner”. He added that “a lot depends” on the US position, but it’s clear there are “many things that matter to all of us”.

The Ukrainian leader’s comments come amid a significant diplomatic fallout with US President Donald Trump, who on Saturday waived expected sanctions targeting Russia’s energy economy and previously called renewed Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure “a disgrace”.

Nonetheless, Zelenskyy said his team is in “virtually nonstop communication” with their US counterparts and said a focus of dialogue is on the results of the talks in Florida and further steps.

US wavers on Ukraine’s access to tech

Also on Sunday, Zelenskyy said he was “thankful” that the US had resumed intelligence sharing with Ukraine after a pause left Ukraine particularly vulnerable to Russia’s regular ballistic missile attacks.

“It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was deblocked by the American side,” Zelenskyy told NBC, adding: “Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days”.

Kyiv has also reported restrictions on the speed of satellite service Starshield, a military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite connectivity network, provided to Ukraine by Musk’s company SpaceX.

Ukraine said its relays were experiencing a limit on how fast receivers could travel while maintaining connectivity, making it almost impossible to intercept Russia’s upgraded jet-powered long-range drones.



Musk had said any restrictions imposed on Starshield connectivity were the responsibility of the US government. The White House quickly rebuked that and in an NBC interview on Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Zelenskyy “very reckless” for accusing the US of throttling connectivity.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that Ukraine is currently blocked from Starshield, and that a request from Kyiv to access the system for attacks deep inside Russia is “under discussion”.

Long-range attacks continue

Also on Sunday, Ukrainian media reported that Russian strikes killed two people in the western Volyn region, near the border with Poland, and injured at least five others across the country. Overnight attacks by Russia killed a woman and injured a six-year-old in the Zaporizhzhia region.

On Saturday night and in the early hours of Sunday, Ukraine hit Russia’s second-largest city, St Petersburg, with a significant drone attack. It targeted a key oil refinery and depot, a warehouse of Russian online retailer Ozon and a data centre run by Russian social media company, VKontakte.

At least one person was killed in the attack, which Russian state media said was the largest on the city since the start of the war in 2022.

World.title: GCC condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as Yemen fighting intensifies
World.content:
Gulf ministers urge action against Houthis as fighting displaces more than 233,000 people across Yemen.

Share GCC condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as Yemen fighting intensifies on social media

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has condemned repeated attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi fighters on Saudi Arabia and pledged support for the kingdom.

The political and economic bloc that includes Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates issued a statement on Sunday, shortly after their foreign ministers’ meeting in Manama, Bahrain.

The statement said an attack on any member affected all six, invoking a joint defence agreement and backing Saudi Arabia’s right to protect itself.

The condemnation came as the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis reported shooting down two drones near Riyadh and in Saudi Arabia‘s Eastern Province early on Sunday.

The coalition said another drone had been intercepted near the capital hours earlier, but did not identify who launched it.

Gulf ministers accused the Houthis of carrying out deadly strikes on civilian airports and vital facilities.

They also pressed for tighter enforcement of a United Nations arms embargo against the group and urged countries to formally designate it “a terrorist organisation”.

The ministers welcomed an October 15 statement from the UN Security Council (UNSC), the body responsible for maintaining international peace, which condemned Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and threats to Red Sea shipping.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government separately appealed to the UNSC to act against Houthi attacks on homes and state facilities.

In letters addressed to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and the UNSC’s president for October, Aglaia Balta, the Yemeni government cited an attack on the presidential palace in Aden, where the government is temporarily based.



Separately on Sunday, UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud in Abu Dhabi to discuss regional security, the UAE’s state news agency WAM reported.

Meanwhile, Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces press offensives on several fronts.

The Yemeni military said the Houthis fired missiles towards the central city of Marib on Sunday, while government troops reported gains in Taiz, further south.

Government-aligned commanders said eight soldiers died in fighting in Lahij province on Saturday.

Government forces also claimed to have killed 12 Houthi fighters in southern Taiz, figures that could not be independently confirmed.

This latest phase of the war followed Houthi gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast last month.

Government forces launched a counteroffensive intended to recapture territory from the Houthis, who seized the capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

Civilians face deepening shortages

The fighting has uprooted more than 233,000 people, according to the International Organization for Migration, the UN’s migration agency.

About 121,000 are in Taiz province, where supply routes have been disrupted by the fighting.

Al Jazeera’s Hadeel al-Yamani, reporting from Taiz, said cooking gas was unavailable and food stocks were dwindling as Houthi forces blocked supplies through the city’s western entrance.

A local office tracking the siege said food prices had risen fivefold.

The World Health Organization, the UN health agency, warned that Taiz’s 12 hospitals had fuel for just four more days and had run out of surgical supplies.

Oxygen and medicines were also critically scarce as the city struggled with a cholera outbreak.

World.title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
World.content:
French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday.

In a national address from the ÃlysÃ©e Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame."

Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted".

Police have arrested about 2,400 people, according to France's interior ministry.

The French president said "nothing justifies" the "unbridled" violence seen and said those involved would face justice.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.

World.title: What we know so far about deadly fire at Canadian military base
World.content:
Four service members are confirmed to have died, Carney said on Sunday.

Officials have confirmed 39 people are in hospital, 19 of whom are in critical conditions.

He also said "dozens" had been "seriously wounded", without providing further information on their conditions.

Prior to Carney addressing the nation, Canadian media reported the death toll as seven citing unnamed military sources.

The prime minister did not indicate whether or not the government expects the death toll to rise.

The names of those who lost their lives have not been identified but their families have been informed.

On Saturday evening, Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton declared a code orange - a disaster response protocol for a high-casualty incident. It was stood down on Sunday afternoon.

Alberta's health service said the emergency response lasted for 10 hours, and involved 22 ambulances and eight aircraft.

Ongoing care for the injured is expected to be "intensive", a statement continued.

A stream of ambulances were seen arriving at the hospital and one doctor told Canadian public broadcaster CBC that the facility had been "completely overwhelmed" by the number of patients.

World.title: Inside Chicago's battle against the synthetic drugs flooding the US
World.content:
Warning: This video contains descriptions of drug-taking and distressing images

A new wave of synthetic drugs is sweeping across the United States, raising fear of a worsening drug crisis.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump pledged a crackdown on drug cartels, proscribing many as terrorist organisations.

Drug overdose deaths have fallen from a peak of around 110,000 in 2022, down to roughly 70,000 last year.

However, America's decades-long drug crisis may be accelerating and authorities are increasingly concerned about cheaper, more powerful synthetic drugs, including an animal tranquilliser called tranq.

The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from the frontlines in South Side, Chicago, where communities are battling the crisis.

Camera journalist: Darren Conway

Read more about the synthetic drug crisis sweeping the US.

World.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
World.content:
At least one person has been killed in an overnight attack on St Petersburg that successfully targeted two of the city's oil facilities.

The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five.

A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit.

Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week.

Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing.

It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

Ukraine has struck St Petersburg before, though regions closer to Ukraine are threatened more often. The city's oil terminal was last hit in July.

Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight into Sunday.

St Petersburg's governor said 12 apartment buildings and two homes were damaged in the attacks on the city, while Pulkovo Airport was temporarily closed.

He also said mobile internet service disruption was possible.

Social network VK confirmed a drone had targeted its regional data centre, but stressed its services were available "as usual" after users reported outages in the early hours of the morning.

Ozon also confirmed its local logistics centre had been targeted by a drone, sparking a fire.

It said staff were evacuated and no one was injured, and that it was not accepting shipments from sellers at the location "as it is currently serving other operational purposes".

As well as numerous oil facilities across Russia, Ukraine has also mounted strikes aimed at disrupting the Russian economy more broadly. Earlier this month, it launched a series of attacks on Yandex, Russia's largest search engine, that led to service disruptions.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have frayed since the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel in the hope of bringing down US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war, ahead of the midterm elections.

Zelensky suggested the deal was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

Trump's decision to temporarily suspend a raft of sanctions against Russia has brought fresh criticism, including from some US Republicans.

However, on Sunday, Zelensky said on Telegram he had had conversations with Trump's top negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

He said their teams are in constant communication and preparing the next diplomatic steps.

Both Russia and Ukraine have been striking one another's energy infrastructure with increasing intensity ahead of the winter, as Moscow's full-scale invasion drags on in its fifth year.

Russia says it hits targets used by Ukraine's military, though the UN noted on Friday that the first two weeks of October had been the deadliest for Ukrainian civilians in years.

Russian strikes on energy facilities have left hundreds of thousands without power, raising concerns about civilians enduring another freezing winter.

Zelensky said on Saturday that tens of thousands of people were still without power. Russia launched nearly 2,700 drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 66 missiles in the past week, most of which were aimed at energy facilities, he said.

World.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
World.content:
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys, while France decried the attack as "appalling". Both called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.

But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened, suggesting it was part of a "co-ordinated campaign to smear Israel".

The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".

It was also condemned by the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".

World.title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
World.content:
Supermodel Cindy Crawford has said she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over the death of her son Presley Gerber.

"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever," she posted on Instagram, next to a black-and-white photo of him. "We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability."

The 27-year-old died on 20 September at a rehab facility in California. Police said officials are investigating his death as a suspected overdose.

Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

Crawford wrote in the post on Sunday: "We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years."

"We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," she also posted.

"Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia," she wrote in closing, with an emoji of angel wings.

The tribute also listed the dates of his birth and death.

The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner lists Gerber's case as pending additional investigation. The Santa Monica Police Department has said there is no indication foul play was involved in his death.

Gerber's sister Kaia also dedicated a post to him on Sunday which included a video of the two siblings as children dancing together, a photo of them standing near the ocean, and a four-page letter to "prez" typed out on a blue background.

In the letter, she said she had been scared of getting her ears pierced, so "you went first".

"But when I held the earring they took from your body, all I could think was: That belongs to you," she wrote.

"I am learning how to love you when I cannot see you," she also wrote. "How to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you. How to be your sister in a world that I can't reach for you in," she wrote.

In recent years, Gerber had spoken openly about his mental health challenges and drug use and frequently posted videos on Instagram himself for what he called "Mental Health Mondays".

His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.

If you're affected by any of the issues in this article you can find details of organisations who can help via the BBC Action Line.

Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide, external, external.

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
World.content:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September.

But Trump issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US national interest, prompting a backlash from US lawmakers. Zelensky said it was unfortunate the US has decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Trump's order was "an important and truly historic moment", and that the sanctions would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Ukraine has accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.

Since then, Ukraine's president declared it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing an EU summit, after Trump said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The sanctions suspension seemed to add further fuel to the fire.

Zelensky said on Saturday morning that the sanctions "could have helped enormously" and that the law was "supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end".

He pointed to Russian overnight attacks on 15 Ukrainian energy facilities that had caused power cuts in several regions and said: "Russia is trying to cause a blackout in Ukraine â right before winter."

Zelensky said it was "important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening" on the ground.

World.title: Anti-government protesters battle with police in Albania
World.content:
Demonstrators and riot police fought pitched battles in the centre of Tirana on Saturday for the fifth day in a row.

Masked protesters, many of them high school and university students, hurled rocks and petrol bombs at riot police trying to defend the education ministry, one of the focal points of the protests.

The police responded with water cannon and volleys of tear gas, sending the crowds scattering. There are also reports that rubber bullets were used for the first time.

Protests which began in the summer have grown into a wider anti-government movement, with calls for the prime minister to resign following corruption allegations linked to his administration.

Many of the protesters in central Tirana wore gas masks or face masks, while volunteers handed out syringes of saline eyewash to reduce the pain from the tear gas which billows down the street.

The constant boom of petrol bombs could be heard exploding on Saturday.

During the afternoon, the focus of the protests shifted to the office of Prime Minister Edi Rama on the city's main boulevard.

Here the crowds swelled to far larger numbers than on previous days.

Riot police faced a steady hail of cobble stones and fireworks, and responded with barrage after barrage of tear gas, some of the canisters landing far back in the crowds, causing panic.

Incensed by the gas, the crowds waited for it to clear, then renewed their attacks.

World.title: ‘Please forgive me’: Fatai Okoya begs billionaire father after 40 years apart
World.content:
More than four decades after becoming estranged from his father, Fatai Okoya has publicly appealed to billionaire industrialist Razaq Akanni Okoya for forgiveness and an opportunity to rebuild their relationship.

Mr Fatai, who identifies himself as the Eleganza Group founder’s first child, appealed in an open letter that circulated online.

He said the years they had spent apart weighed heavily on him and urged his father to allow them to make peace while they still had time.

“More than four decades have passed, and today, I write with a humble heart, putting aside all pride to say: Dad, I am truly sorry. Please, find it in your heart to forgive me,” he wrote.

The letter, signed “Your First Child, Fatai Okoya,” has generated reactions online, with some people expressing sympathy and others questioning what caused the prolonged estrangement.

‘Pain of separation’

Mr Fatai said he had made previous attempts to reach his father and resolve their differences, but the separation continued to cause him pain.

“Over the years, I have tried to reach out and make peace because the pain of our separation and the precious years we have lost weigh heavily on my heart,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“No matter what has happened, you remain my father, and I will forever be your first child.”

He asked Mr Okoya to look beyond the events that separated them, saying they could not recover the years already lost but could decide what happened next.

“Dad, we cannot turn back the hands of time, but we can choose to make the years ahead different,” he wrote.

“Life is precious, time waits for no one, and I do not want us to lose any more opportunities to love, forgive and reconnect.”

Although Mr Fatai repeatedly referred to past pain and differences, he did not explain what caused the rift or why the separation lasted for more than four decades.

‘Let us begin again’

Mr Fatai said he wanted a chance to heal their relationship and restore their bond.

“I am simply asking for a chance a chance to heal, to make peace and to rebuild the bond between a father and his child,” he wrote.

He said he was prepared to pursue reconciliation with humility and an open mind.

“Dad, please, let love speak louder than the pain of the past. Let forgiveness open a door that has been closed for far too long. I am ready to take that step with humility, sincerity and an open heart.”

He ended the letter with another apology, saying that despite their years apart, he still wanted his father back in his life.

“I love you, Dad. I miss you, and deep down, I still long for the blessing of having my father back in my life,” he wrote.

“Dad, I am truly sorry. My heart is open, my hands are extended, and my hope for reconciliation remains alive. Please, let us begin again.”

The Okoya family

Razaq Okoya founded the Eleganza Group, a manufacturing conglomerate known for producing household and consumer goods.

He began his business career as a trader before expanding into manufacturing and establishing Eleganza in the early 1970s.

The industrialist has a large family, although the precise number of his children has not been publicly confirmed by him.

In February 2026, one of his sons, Raheem Okoya, popularly known as Siraheem, said in an interview that his father had 26 children with nine women.

The singer described himself as the 23rd child and said the eldest was about 60 years old.

However, the information available for this report does not independently establish Mr Fatai’s claim that he is the billionaire’s first child.

Mr Fatai’s mother’s identity also remains unclear. He did not name her in the letter, and PREMIUM TIMES found no reliable public record identifying her.

The circumstances surrounding the estrangement also remain unclear. Beyond saying he had previously sought peace, Mr Fatai did not provide details of his reported attempts to contact his father.

As of the time of this report, Mr Okoya had not publicly responded to the letter.

World.title: Presidency disputes Makinde’s claim of N250 billion NLNG dividends per state
World.content:
The presidency has disputed Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s claim that the federal government is withholding N250 billion in Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas Limited (NLNG) dividends meant for each state, describing the allegation as “false.”

Bayo Onanuga, special adviser to President Bola Tinubu on information and strategy, said in a statement on Sunday that the amount claimed by the governor was inconsistent with the revenue-sharing formula and the history of NLNG’s dividend payments to the Federation.

Mr Onanuga argued that a one-off payment of N250 billion to each of Nigeria’s 36 states would amount to N9 trillion, excluding the federal government, the Federal Capital Territory and the 774 local government areas.

“Under the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) formula, states receive 26.72 per cent of the distributable Federation Account revenue. For the states’ share alone to reach N9 trillion, total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed N33.68 trillion (about $25 billion) in a single declaration,” the statement read. “NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout.”

Mr Onanuga urged the public to disregard the claim. “Makinde’s latest claim that the Federal Government is withholding the NLNG dividend windfall is false and should be disregarded.”

However, the presidency’s statement did not provide a transaction-by-transaction reconciliation of the specific NLNG dividend proceeds referenced by Mr Makinde or a breakdown of the sums allegedly due to individual states.

The dispute followed remarks by Mr Makinde at the 2027 Budget Stakeholders’ Consultative Engagement in Ibadan on Friday, where he alleged that the Federal Government had spent the dividend proceeds instead of distributing the states’ shares.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“They fooled us. The Nigeria LNG paid dividends to the Federal Government, which went straight into the Federation Account, but they spent it,” Mr Makinde said,

He stated that the amounts due to the states had been reconciled and that each state was expected to receive more than N250 billion.

Mr Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement for the upcoming 2027 elections, further alleged that the release of the funds had been postponed until after the 2027 general elections, questioning why political considerations should take precedence over the needs of citizens.

“Each state was supposed to get N250 billion. We had already identified projects that would expand Oyo State’s economy. But they have now said the money will not be paid until after the election. Is the election more important than the people of Nigeria?” the governor said.

Presidency’s argument

Responding, Mr Onanuga said states receive 26.72 per cent of distributable Federation Account revenue under the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) sharing formula.

He argued that for the states’ combined share to reach N9 trillion, the total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed N33.68 trillion ($25 billion), in a single declaration.

“NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout,” the presidency’s statement read.

According to the statement, NLNG has paid approximately $21.5 billion in dividends to the Federation over the past 25 years, with less than $3 billion realised since Mr Tinubu assumed office.

Mr Onanuga argued that the amount allegedly being withheld would therefore exceed the company’s entire historical dividend payments to the Federation.

“Therefore, any claim that a single payout exceeds the company’s entire lifetime distribution to the Federation—and is being withheld—defies basic logic and economic reality,” he said.

World.title: Protect indigenous seeds, farmers’ rights, HOMEF tells FG on World Food Day
World.content:
The Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF), an environmental advocacy organisation, has called on the federal government to protect indigenous seeds and farmers’ rights, warning that industrial agricultural practices and restrictive seed policies could undermine food sovereignty, biodiversity, and nutrition.

The organisation made the call on Friday to mark World Food Day, observed annually on 16 October, arguing that hunger and malnutrition persist in resource-rich countries because of political and economic choices that disadvantage smallholder farmers and local food systems.

In a statement made available to PREMIUM TIMES by its Media and Communications Manager, Kome Odhomor, HOMEF said food security requires more than increasing agricultural output. It called for policies that protect local seed varieties, promote ecological farming and give farming communities greater control over what they grow and how they produce food.

The organisation also called on Nigerians to pay closer attention to the origins and nutritional quality of their food, warning that climate change, economic instability, and conflict continue to threaten food production and distribution.

Food sovereignty

Nnimmo Bassey, HOMEF’s executive director, said Nigeria’s food system was overly dependent on monoculture and cash-crop production, which he noted weakened food supply chains, depleted soil health and reduced farmers’ control over agricultural production.

“World Food Day should be a day of reflection. It must also be a day of structural reckoning,” Mr Bassey said, calling for a shift from industrial uniformity towards diverse and ecologically sustainable farming systems.

He said indigenous seeds are critical to adapting to climate change because they preserve genetic diversity that can support drought resistance, pest management, and improved nutrition.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We must move beyond the short-sighted goal of ‘yield at any cost’ and support a transition to agroecology,” he said.

Agroecology applies ecological principles to agricultural production, emphasising soil health, biodiversity, local knowledge, and sustainable relationships between farming communities and their environment.

Mr Bassey said protecting indigenous seeds was essential to preventing biodiversity loss and sustaining ecosystems, arguing that food systems should not sacrifice environmental health for short-term production gains.

Seed laws, farmers’ rights

HOMEF’s Director of Programmes, Joyce Brown, said hunger in resource-rich African countries reflected failures in political and economic decision-making.

She said that food should not be treated merely as a commodity for profit but as a fundamental human right connected to public health, cultural identity and community livelihoods.

Ms Brown called on governments and international institutions to review policies that, she said, privilege industrial exporters over small-scale farmers who supply local communities.

She specifically raised concerns about Nigeria’s Plant Variety Protection Act, 2021, explaining that restrictions on farmers’ ability to save and reuse seeds could threaten the food and nutritional security of vulnerable communities.

The law provides a framework for protecting the rights of breeders of new plant varieties. The debate over its implementation includes questions about how breeders’ rights should be balanced with farmers’ traditional practices and access to seeds.

Ms Brown said agricultural policies should recognise farmers’ rights and ensure that communities closest to the land retain meaningful authority over what they grow and how they use their resources.

‘Industrial agriculture not the only solution’

Mariann Bassey-Olsson, deputy director of Environmental Rights Action/Friends of the Earth Nigeria, described seed-saving and exchange as essential to farmers’ independence and the preservation of cultural heritage.

She rejected the argument that industrial agriculture was the only viable way to feed the world, saying smallholder farmers had sustained communities for generations through locally adapted farming practices.

Ms Bassey-Olsson said indigenous seeds embodied generations of farmers’ knowledge and adaptation to local soils and climatic conditions.

She warned that losing control of local seed varieties could make farmers increasingly dependent on foreign corporations and weaken their ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions.

She also opposed genetically modified crops, saying it could threaten farmers’ seed rights and biodiversity and increase dependence on foreign companies.

Her position reflects HOMEF’s call for increased investment in agroecology and locally controlled food systems, rather than approaches that put industrial agricultural interests at the centre of food production.

Food security, climate change

HOMEF said future food systems should prioritise nutritional quality, environmental sustainability and farmers’ livelihoods, rather than focus narrowly on increasing yields.

It called for better access to agricultural knowledge, tools and resources for smallholder farmers and marginalised communities, warning that climate change and other socioeconomic pressures could further destabilise food supplies.

The organisation also asked governments to support diverse local food systems that can withstand climate shocks while protecting biodiversity and improving soil health.

World Food Day is an annual international observance that raises awareness of hunger and food insecurity and promotes access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food.

World.title: NCDMB, Heritage Energy train 48 Nigerians in subsea engineering
World.content:
The Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), in partnership with Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited (HEOSL) and Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited, has launched a Human Capacity Development programme to train 48 Nigerians in subsea engineering.

The kick-off ceremony took place on Friday, 16 October, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, as part of the Board’s efforts to address critical skills gaps and strengthen indigenous technical expertise in the oil and gas industry.

The programme combines six months of classroom instruction with six months of structured on-the-job training, giving participants specialised knowledge and practical experience in subsea engineering. The curriculum covers risers and hydrodynamics engineering, offshore structures design and engineering, pipeline engineering, and computer-aided design and drafting (AutoCAD).

In his keynote address, the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, Felix Omatsola Ogbe, a Fellow of Nigerian Society of Engineers, represented by the General Manager, Human Capacity Development, Ms Emelle Alexis, said the programme would equip the trainees with the technical expertise required for complex subsea operations and the safe, efficient and reliable operation of modern oil and gas facilities.

“Today marks the beginning of a transformational journey for 48 young Nigerians in a highly specialised field that demands precision, discipline and accountability. Through intensive classroom instruction and structured on-the-job training, the participants will gain hands-on experience in subsea engineering,” he said.

Ogbe stressed that subsea operations require technical competence, professionalism and an unwavering commitment to safety.

“The competencies you acquire through this programme are critical to the safe, efficient, reliable and environmentally responsible operation of modern oil and gas facilities. Beyond technical proficiency, the training is designed to develop your problem-solving skills, teamwork, professionalism and commitment to safety,” he stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Executive Secretary urged the trainees to make the most of the opportunity and demonstrate the discipline and commitment required to succeed in the industry. He expressed confidence that they would emerge with the skills and professional standards needed to contribute to the sector.

In his remarks, the Manager, Nigerian Content Development at Heritage Energy, Felix Osiwo, reaffirmed the company’s commitment to indigenous skills development. He noted that a skilled Nigerian workforce is essential to delivering current and future energy infrastructure projects and sustaining industry growth.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Managing Director of Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited, George Ebuh, represented by Ifedolapo Aderibigbe, described the programme as a strategic investment by Heritage Energy, NCDMB and Global Oceon in developing indigenous subsea engineering expertise. He noted that skilled local professionals are vital to the safe and reliable operation of offshore and deepwater infrastructure.

The trainees expressed appreciation for the opportunity to acquire specialised subsea engineering skills, identifying safety training and AutoCAD as important areas of learning. The programme is part of NCDMB’s Top 10 Field Readiness Human Capacity Development initiatives, designed to address critical skills gaps in the oil and gas industry. It supports the Board’s efforts to develop specialised Nigerian expertise for offshore and deepwater operations, facilitate technology transfer and increase local participation in high-value industry activities.

The ceremony was attended by representatives of NCDMB, Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited and Global Oceon Engineers Nigeria Limited, as well as the trainees, facilitators and other industry stakeholders.

World.title: Utomi says Akwa Ibom ex-governor Victor Attah has attained ‘immortality’
World.content:
Nigerian professor, entrepreneur, and former presidential candidate Pat Utomi has described Akwa Ibom State’s Governor Victor Attah as a leader who has attained “immortality”, citing the enduring influence of his development vision.

Mr Utomi, also a professor of entrepreneurship at Lagos Business School, assessed this in a Facebook post on Friday after travelling from Ikot Ekpene to Victor Attah International Airport to welcome former President Olusegun Obasanjo for the unveiling of a media platform in Uyo.

Reflecting on the journey, Mr Utomi said the experience reminded him of the foundations Mr Attah laid during his eight-year tenure as governor and how his development initiatives continued to influence the state beyond his time in office.

“I was reminded of the foundation that one decent, visionary man of character, Obong Victor Attah, laid as Governor of Akwa Ibom State, and the fruits of his labour, so evident even in the work of his successors, both good and bad,” he wrote.

Mr Utomi said the experience gave him a renewed appreciation of transformational leadership, particularly the ability to envision a future beyond immediate political considerations and persevere in pursuing it despite opposition.

“These are the people who see tomorrow and persevere to bring it about, even in the face of determined opposition,” he said.

He added that Mr Attah had “attained immortality, like Chief Obafemi Awolowo, Dr Michael Okpara and Sir Ahmadu Bello,” while continuing to live simply.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Attah’s enduring legacy

Mr Attah, an architect and politician, governed Akwa Ibom from 29 May 1999 to 29 May 2007, becoming one of the principal figures in the state’s development following Nigeria’s return to civil rule in 1999.

His administration pursued major infrastructure and economic development projects, including establishing an international airport, the Ibom Power Plant, developing the Ibom Hotels and Golf Resort, and planning an Ibom Deep Seaport. The state later renamed the airport Victor Attah International Airport in 2018 to recognise his contributions to the state.

Mr Attah initiated the Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility at Victor Attah International Airport. Still, the project was abandoned before his successor, Udom Emmanuel, revived it and inaugurated it in May 2023.

Subsequent reports showed that outstanding construction and operational requirements remained under Governor Umo Eno, whose administration was still pursuing a partnership to bring the facility into full operation in August 2026.

Beyond infrastructure, Mr Attah became a prominent advocate of resource control and fiscal federalism, insisting that oil-producing states should receive a fairer share of revenue generated from their natural resources.

His advocacy was particularly noteworthy in the Niger Delta, where communities and state governments had long demanded more benefits from petroleum wealth extracted from the region.

The struggle over derivation revenue became a major constitutional and political issue during the administration of Mr Obasanjo, who was president from 1999 to 2007, the same period Mr Attah governed Akwa Ibom.

Mr Attah’s campaign for resource control helped put revenue allocation and the rights of oil-producing states at the centre of national debate. The constitutional principle of derivation provides for a share of revenue from natural resources to be returned to the areas from which the resources are derived.

READ ALSO: Utomi faces backlash over defence of Kila despite academic credentials controversy

Beyond monuments

Mr Utomi’s remarks place Mr Attah’s legacy within a bigger debate about the meaning of leadership and how political performance should be assessed after an administration leaves office.

By comparing the former governor with Awolowo, Okpara and Ahmadu Bello, Mr Utomi suggested that a leader’s lasting importance lies not only in the projects completed during his tenure, but also in the institutions, ideas and development pathways that survive him.

Late Awolowo, the former premier of Western Nigeria, was associated with major social welfare and education programmes. Okpara, who led the former Eastern Region, was known for agricultural and industrial development. At the same time, Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto, was a central political figure in Northern Nigeria’s development and administration.

Mr Utomi’s assessment goes beyond the physical infrastructure associated with Mr Attah’s administration. It frames the former governor’s legacy by how far his vision continued to shape the state under successive governments.

However, Mr Utomi’s tribute was a personal assessment of Mr Attah’s leadership, rather than a comprehensive evaluation of the former governor’s record.

Mr Attah, born on 20 November 1938, turned 87 in November 2025. His political and professional career has continued to attract public attention, including at the 2025 launch of a biography chronicling his life and career.

World.title: LASU professor Tunde Akanni inducted as peace studies fellow
World.content:
Tunde Akanni of Lagos State University (LASU) has been inducted as a Fellow of the Society for Peace Studies and Practice (SPSP).

Mr Akanni, a professor of Journalism in LASU’s Faculty of Communication and Media Studies, received the fellowship at the society’s 20th International Conference and General Assembly held at Lead City University, Ibadan, from 5 to 9 October 2026.

The fellowship recognises his contributions to journalism, conflict-sensitive communication and development communication, according to reports on the investiture.

FCCPC congratulates Akanni

The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), where Mr Akanni is currently on sabbatical, also congratulated him on the recognition.

In a letter dated 7 October 2026, the commission described the fellowship as a testament to his scholarly contributions to journalism and his commitment to conflict-sensitive journalism.

The letter, signed by Yisau Adepoju, Head of the Administration Department, on behalf of the FCCPC’s Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Olatunji Bello, said Mr Akanni had consistently demonstrated commitment to development communication and its role in promoting social change.

The commission said the recognition was “timely and richly deserved”, and expressed confidence that Mr Akanni would continue to contribute to Nigeria and the global academic community.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This auspicious milestone is a clear testimony to your laudable scholarly contributions to the field of journalism. As a thoroughbred professional and accomplished academic, you have consistently demonstrated passion and unwavering commitment to the promotion of Conflict- Sensitive Journalism. You have tenaciously identified with this strand of Development Communication that is renowned for fostering sustainable social change and advancing the overall quality of life, particularly in developing nations,” FCCPC noted.

About Tunde Akanni

Mr Akanni is a Professor of Journalism at LASU. The university’s official academic profile lists his specialisation as Journalism and Development Communications and his PhD in Media and Conflict Resolution Studies from the University of Ibadan.

He joined LASU’s Department of Journalism in 2001 as an Assistant Lecturer and rose through the academic ranks. In March 2025, the university’s Governing Council approved his elevation to full professor of Journalism and Development Communication. At the time, he was an Associate Professor and pioneer Director of LASU’s Digital Media Research Centre.

Before joining academia, Mr Akanni worked in Nigeria’s print media industry, including at The Punch and National Concord, where he rose to Acting Features Editor. Following the proscription of Concord titles in 1994, he became Head of Campaigns at the Civil Liberties Organisation.

His academic interests include journalism practice, media ethics, development communication, political communication, media and conflict, strategic communication and the impact of artificial intelligence on media systems.

He has undertaken academic and professional training at institutions including Columbia University in the United States, the University of Leicester in the United Kingdom and the Institute of Social Studies in The Hague, Netherlands. He is also a British Chevening Scholar and a recipient of the Netherlands NUFFIC Fellowship.

World.title: Court of Appeal upholds N12m damages against EFCC over Ubani’s detention
World.content:
The Court of Appeal in Abuja has dismissed an appeal by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) challenging a judgement awarding Monday Ubani, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), N12 million in compensation for his unlawful detention in 2019.

Delivering judgement on the appeal on Thursday, a three-member panel of judges unanimously upheld the award.

The appellate court also ordered the commission to pay N300,000 in costs, according to a statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday.

Mr Ubani, a lawyer and former vice-president of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), was not yet a SAN when the EFCC detained him in March 2019. He attained the rank in 2024.

How the dispute began

The dispute began after the EFCC declared Ngozi Olejeme, a former chairperson of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), wanted over allegations of financial crimes relating to her time at the agency.

Mr Ubani said he helped persuade her to return to Nigeria to answer the allegations. She was subsequently granted administrative bail, with him and former Senator Christopher Enai standing as sureties.

A surety guarantees that a person granted bail will comply with the conditions of their release, including appearing when required by investigators or a court.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, the EFCC later said it could no longer reach Ms Olejeme and demanded that her sureties produce her. The commission arrested Mr Ubani and Mr Enai in March 2019.

Mr Ubani maintained that he was not responsible for her disappearance. He said he had helped bring her back to Nigeria and questioned why the commission held him responsible after its operatives visited her home and could no longer reach her.

Later that month, Judge Sylvanus Oriji of the FCT High Court in Apo ordered the EFCC to charge the two men in court or release them on bail. The judge also granted them bail subject to conditions.

However, the commission did not comply with the order by the deadline, prompting their lawyer, Mike Ozekhome, also a SAN, to initiate contempt proceedings against the then acting EFCC chairman, Ibrahim Magu.

In January 2022, Judge Oriji ruled that the EFCC’s arrest and detention of Mr Ubani violated his fundamental rights.

The judge held that a surety could be required to show cause or forfeit the bail bond if the person for whom they stood surety could not be produced, rather than being arrested and detained.

Consequently, he declared the detention illegal and awarded Mr Ubani N12 million in damages but declined to order the EFCC to issue a public apology.

Dissatisfied with the judgment, the commission appealed to the Court of Appeal, challenging the trial court’s jurisdiction and the amount awarded as compensation.

The appellate court has now dismissed the appeal and upheld the trial court’s jurisdiction.

World.title: ﻿Stakeholders say poor healthcare coordination leaves patients to navigate care alone
World.content:
Poor coordination across Nigeria’s healthcare system leaves patients and their families navigating referrals, carrying medical records between facilities, and repeatedly explaining their medical histories as they seek treatment.

Addressing these gaps was a central focus of discussions at the 2026 Health Equity Conference, where stakeholders called for stronger referral systems, improved information sharing and clearer responsibility for patients as they move between healthcare providers.

Speaking at the conference, Yemi Ajao, Chief Executive Officer of OneBarrow International Limited, said patients should not have to navigate the gaps between hospitals, laboratories, pharmacies and specialist services without adequate guidance.

Mr Ajao said information and responsibility for care must follow patients as they move between providers, warning that poor communication and weak referral processes could leave them uncertain about where to seek further treatment.

“A patient does not experience healthcare as a collection of professional mandates, institutional departments or organisational charts. A patient experiences a journey,” he said.

He urged stakeholders to identify the institutional and operational barriers preventing patients from receiving coordinated care across different facilities and levels of the health system.

The conference, held from 13 to 15 October, was themed ‘Care Coordination as the Core Engine of Health Equity’. It brought together representatives of government, healthcare institutions, professional associations and other sectors to discuss ways to improve access to healthcare.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Making referrals work

To illustrate the coordination gaps, Mr Ajao presented a patient scenario involving a woman named Amina. He asked participants to consider what happens when a patient is referred from one healthcare provider to another.

He asked whether patients knew where to go after receiving a referral, whether the receiving provider had the information needed to deliver appropriate care, and whether anyone followed up to confirm the referral was completed.

He said these questions should inform decisions about healthcare policies, financing, and technology.

The scenario highlighted the importance of treating care as a connected process rather than a series of isolated encounters with different providers.

When referral information isn’t shared effectively, or follow-up responsibilities are unclear, patients may have to coordinate their own treatment, complicating access to appropriate care.

Mr Ajao said the conference aims to examine patient journeys, institutional responsibilities, financing, partnerships, data, and implementation through plenary discussions and policy laboratories.

He urged participants to recognise the constraints facing institutions while identifying practical measures to improve coordination and continuity of care.

He called for collaboration among government agencies, regulators, healthcare professionals, private organisations and civil society to address gaps in service delivery.

According to him, effective referrals, timely information sharing and clear responsibility for patients’ care could help improve the healthcare experience and restore public confidence in the system.

“National pride grows when people can see their country working for them,” he said.

Reforms must improve patients’ access

Also speaking at the conference, Adijah Elijah, Director of Health Planning, Research and Statistics at the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, said government policies and investments must translate into tangible improvements in access to healthcare.

Mrs Elijah said Nigeria’s commitment to achieving universal health coverage by 2030 would require government institutions, healthcare providers, development partners and communities to work towards shared priorities.

“Health equity is both a moral imperative and a practical investment in Nigeria’s human capital, productivity and sustainable development,” she said.

She identified the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Sector-Wide Approach as frameworks for aligning investments, strengthening coordination and improving accountability across the health sector.

However, she said the effectiveness of the health system should not be measured solely by the number of facilities established, the resources committed or the policies adopted.

Rather, she said, progress should also be assessed by whether people could obtain quality healthcare without suffering financial hardship.

Mrs Elijah urged stakeholders to prioritise implementation and measurable improvements in access, particularly for underserved populations.

World.title: Mbappe scores brace as Real Madrid thrash Sevilla 4-1
World.content:
Real Madrid’s French forward #10 Kylian Mbappe celebrates with teammates scoring his team’s third goal from the penalty spot during the Spanish league football match between Real Madrid CF and Sevilla FC at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium in Madrid on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Kylian Mbappe scored twice including one brilliant individual goal as Real Madrid thrashed Sevilla 4-1 on Sunday to climb into third in La Liga.

Arda Guler netted a spectacular opener before Mbappe’s double and a rocket from Yan Diomande as Jose Mourinho side moved above Real Betis, who lost 5-2 to league leaders Barcelona on Saturday.

Mbappe’s first was a sensational strike, involving a roulette on the edge of Sevilla’s box, and his second a chipped Panenka penalty.

Champions Barca are six points ahead of Real Madrid before next weekend’s Clasico at Camp Nou, with Atletico Madrid second, sandwiched between Spain’s giants.

Mourinho lined up with Diomande on the left in place of suspended Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, and brought Guler in as part of the midfield pivot.

Vinicius’s red card for hair-pulling last weekend provoked ire in the Spanish capital at officiating in Spain.

Madrid fans at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium chanted and held up banners against La Liga president Javier Tebas, after he said the club’s strategy of trying to discredit referees was similar to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.

Los Blancos and their new coach Mourinho have complained bitterly about Spanish refereeing in recent weeks, and more generally over the past two seasons, in which they have failed to win a major trophy.

On this occasion it was Sevilla who had more to complain about in terms of officiating as Madrid eased to victory.

A quiet start was disrupted when Madrid midfielder Guler appeared to elbow Sevilla’s Peque, which went unpunished midway through the first half.

Sevilla had resisted the probing of Madrid’s attacking stars early on, but were undone by a moment of magic from Guler himself after 30 minutes.

Jude Bellingham played the ball out to the flank where record signing Diomande received it and fed Guler on the edge of the box.

The Turkish playmaker lofted a superb strike across Sevilla goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos and into the top corner.

– Mbappe skill –

Mbappe came close to adding a second with a lightning-quick burst down the pitch, but his low effort was saved.

The French superstar soon got his goal, one of the best of the season.

Bellingham backheeled the ball into Mbappe’s path and the forward produced a dazzling roulette turn into the area, before showing more skill to rapidly sidestep the goalkeeper and roll home.

Mbappe extended the lead from the penalty spot after he went down under a light touch from Andres Castrin in the area.

The forward, who hopes to be crowned the best player in the world at the Ballon d’Or ceremony later in October, dinked home his ninth league goal of the season.

Sevilla pulled one back with a neat strike from Manuel Bueno, but there was no fightback on the cards.

Ivorian winger Diomande thumped home from outside of the box for his second goal since joining this summer from RB Leipzig, Madrid’s next opponents in the Champions League.

Earlier, Real Sociedad rose to fifth with a thumping 5-2 win at bottom side Malaga, Celta Vigo defeated Alaves 2-1 and Osasuna beat Racing Santander 2-0.
