World.title: Foreign Media Bash Torcida following Ajax Incident
World.content:
October the 17th, 2026 – Foreign media from a multitude of countries have bashed Torcida following the violent clash with Ajax in Split.

Antisemitic and Nazi chants by some Torcida members during the recent procession towards Poljud, a coffin with the inscription Ajax on it, and the interruption of the match due to pyrotechnics have resonated with the foreign media. Index reports that media outlets from Israel and the Netherlands to Germany, Poland and Russia, as well as numerous media outlets in neighbouring countries, wrote about the incidents in Split.

The most attention was attracted by the chants “Crush, crush the Jews”, “Auschwitz, Auschwitz”, “Rise, Adolf” and “Come on, come on, Ustaše”, which were heard during Torcida’s cortege ahead of the Hajduk–Ajax match in the Conference League. At the head of the procession was a yellow Golf with a coffin on the roof on which “Ajax” was written. The match itself did not pass without incidents either. The encounter at Poljud was interrupted in the 77th minute after home fans lit a large quantity of pyrotechnics. Because of the dense smoke the players left the pitch, and the match was resumed after 12 minutes. Hajduk won 2–1.

“shocking antisemitism”

Israel’s Ynet, one of the most-read portals in the country, published an article under the title “Auschwitz, Auschwitz: Antisemitism against the ‘Jewish club’ and its Israeli player”. The portal describes Torcida’s procession towards the stadium and the antisemitic chants shouted by individual fans. It particularly highlights the mentions of Auschwitz and Adolf Hitler, as well as the coffin with the inscription Ajax. On Thursday afternoon, before the start of the match, Israeli Israel Hayom published an article under the title “Auschwitz, crush the Jews: Shocking antisemitism against Oscar Gloukh”.

The paper states that the Hajduk–Ajax match was overshadowed by antisemitic and violent incidents and reports the chants “Crush the Jews”, “Auschwitz, Auschwitz”, “Rise, Adolf” and “Come on, Ustaše”.

Both Israeli media particularly emphasise Ajax’s historical connection with the Jewish community in Amsterdam. Part of Ajax’s fans have for decades used the name “Super Jews” and Jewish symbols as part of their supporter identity. That tradition developed, among other things, as a response to antisemitic insults from fans of rival clubs. Most Ajax fans who use that symbolism are not Jewish, but because of it the Dutch club is often the target of antisemitic messages from opposing fans. Israeli media also stress that their national-team player Oscar Gloukh plays for Ajax. Israel Hayom also reported on earlier attacks on Dutch fans, including two who sought medical help because of minor injuries, and on 57 people arrested after the riots in Split.

“disgusting insults”

The scandalous Torcida chants were also reported by the respected British The Telegraph, which published an article under the title “Croatian football fans chanted disgusting antisemitic insults”. The Telegraph also recalls the riots in Split during which the police detained dozens of fans, as well as the violence in Amsterdam in November 2024 linked to the Ajax–Maccabi Tel Aviv match. The British medium places the events in the broader context of earlier racist incidents in Croatian football. It recalls that the Croatian Football Federation has been fined several times over the years because of fans’ behaviour, including incidents at the Croatia–France match in March 2025.

“they showed themselves in the worst possible light”

The Dutch football portal FCUpdate published an article under the title “Scandalous chanting at the Hajduk Split – Ajax match”. “Hajduk Split fans showed themselves in the worst light ahead of the Conference League match against Ajax,” the Dutch portal writes.

FCUpdate states that a large group of Croatian fans on the way to the stadium sang shocking songs. “Videos are circulating on social networks in which dozens of Hajduk Split fans can be seen and heard singing antisemitic and Nazi songs on the way to the stadium,” the portal states. The Dutch medium reports the chants about Jews, Auschwitz and Hitler, and particularly singles out the coffin with the inscription Ajax. “But that was not the end,” FCUpdate writes, stating that the fans displayed a coffin with the name of the Dutch club which was later destroyed. FCUpdate also reports that the Croatian police have launched a criminal investigation because of the disputed chants during the cortege.

“they changed about auschwitz”

The scandal was also reported by the large Polish sports portal Przegląd Sportowy. The title of the article published late last night reads: “Rise, Adolf. They chanted about Auschwitz. Behaviour in the Conference League resonated”. The Polish medium particularly emphasises that Hajduk fans repeated the provocation from 1995, when Hajduk and Ajax played in the Champions League quarter-finals. Even then the fans carried a coffin with the inscription Ajax, and 31 years later they staged a similar scene again.

“Shocking scenes in Split before the Hajduk–Ajax match in the Conference League. Croatian fans repeated a horrific gesture from 31 years ago, encouraged violence against Jews and shouted antisemitic slogans,” Przegląd Sportowy writes. The portal reports the chants about Auschwitz, Hitler and the Ustaše, and particularly stresses that open glorification of Nazism was recorded during the cortege. It also reports the police statement about the investigation because of punishable chants during the procession.

the torcida scandal made it to the green, romanian and even chilean media

Torcida’s antisemitic chanting was also carried by numerous Greek media. The Greek public broadcaster ERT published an article under the title “Horrific Nazi chants and a coffin with the inscription Ajax during the procession of Hajduk fans”, while the sports portal Gazzetta wrote about “the coffin and Nazi chants of Hajduk fans”.

The incidents were also reported by the Romanian sports daily Gazeta Sporturilor, which published a text under the title “Rise, Adolf, light the ovens! Horrifying scenes in the Conference League, they disgraced themselves in front of Europe!” The Romanian medium describes the antisemitic chants and recalls the similar provocation with the coffin during the Hajduk–Ajax encounter back in 1995. The news also reached South America. Chilean Cooperativa reported on Nazi and antisemitic chants against Ajax, stating that Croatian fans shouted slogans about Jews, Auschwitz and Hitler and carried a coffin with the name of the Dutch club.

the german and even russian media weigh in

Unlike the Israeli, Dutch and Polish media, German reports mostly focused on the events during the match. Berlin’s Tagesspiegel carried the news of the German news agency dpa under the title “Defeat and interruption because of pyrotechnics: A bitter evening for ter Stegen”. The German agency writes that Ajax experienced a bitter start to the Conference League and that the match was close to a definitive interruption because of the mass use of pyrotechnics by home fans. Russian media, including RBC, Sport-Ekspress and Euro-Football, also reported on the interruption. In their reports the emphasis was also on the flare display, dense smoke and interruption of the match, while RBC also mentioned earlier fan clashes and extremist chants in Split.

regional media

Numerous regional media outlets also reported on the antisemitic chanting. The Serbian public broadcaster RTS published an article under the title “Scandal in Split – Hajduk fans sang ‘Auschwitz, Auschwitz’ and ‘Rise, Adolf’”. The Montenegrin public broadcaster RTCG also reported on the antisemitic chanting, while the Macedonian Sloboden pečat published a text and a recording of the events. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, the scandal was carried by N1, Vijesti.ba and SportSport.ba, which even before the start of the match published a report on the cortege. Slovenian Siol reported on fan clashes in Split and police interventions, while Dnevnik carried information about the antisemitic chanting.

apologies from hajduk split

Split police confirmed that during Torcida’s cortege they recorded chants that have the characteristics of punishable behaviour and that they are conducting a criminal investigation in order to establish the circumstances and identify those responsible. After the match Hajduk also reacted, apologising for the behaviour of part of the fans who caused the interruption of the encounter by the mass use of pyrotechnics.

“We apologise to the competition organiser as well as to the management and players of Ajax who witnessed scenes by which we do not want Europe to remember us,” Hajduk stated. The club added that it had taken all prescribed measures, but that despite that something happened of which it is not proud and that it is ready to bear responsibility. Hajduk’s apology referred to the events at the stadium. The police are separately investigating the antisemitic and Nazi chants during the cortege.

World.title: Eesti 200 and Greens will not merge
World.content:
Eesti 200 decided at its council meeting Sunday not to merge with the non-parliamentary Estonian Greens ahead of the 2027 general elections.

While consultations had previously been held on a possible merger, Eesti 200 has now decided not to enter into merger negotiations with the Greens. The coalition party's head of communications, Johannes Merilai, said the Greens' policies differ from those of Eesti 200 and that a merger would add nothing to the party's core identity, which is based on progressive and liberal views.

"They have strong positions on certain issues, but if we were to bring the two parties together, it's not clear whether that would add anything," Merilai said.

He noted that Sunday's meeting did not address whether Eesti 200 would participate in next spring's Riigikogu elections. "There is still time to make that decision. There's no need to rush," Merilai said. He added that the party is currently preparing for the elections and aims to field a full slate of candidates. However, no final decision was made on Sunday.

Toomas Uibo, chairman of Eesti 200's Riigikogu parliamentary group, announced in a social media comment on Thursday that he does not intend to run in the next Riigikogu elections. Fellow party member Irja Lutsar announced similar plans in July, although just three and a half months ago, party leader Kristina Kallas said that, to her knowledge, all Eesti 200 MPs were prepared to run for reelection.

The latest weekly poll conducted by the Institute for Societal Studies (MTÜ Ühiskonnauuringute Instituut) and polling firm Norstat Eesti AS showed support for Eesti 200 at 1.2 percent.

World.title: Janno Jakobson: Speaking Estonian not the same as teaching Estonian
World.content:
Students do not choose their parents, the language spoken at home or their socioeconomic background, but teachers can choose how they support students and what learning opportunities they provide, writes Janno Jakobson.

The transition to Estonian-language education is one of the most significant changes in Estonia's education system. No one questions its necessity anymore, but are we, as adults, prepared to make enough of an effort to ensure its success? We are demanding increasingly better Estonian-language skills from students learning Estonian as a second language, but are we also creating the conditions they need to achieve this?

In discussions with colleagues from different schools, one point keeps coming up: The problem is not always a lack of skills among teachers, but rather how existing knowledge and skills are applied in everyday teaching.

Imagine a student who spends an entire school day in Estonian-language classes. The teacher speaks Estonian, the textbooks are in Estonian and the student completes exercises in a workbook. By the end of the day, however, the student has spoken only a handful of sentences in Estonian. Does such a school day do enough to support the student's language development?

To acquire a language, students must have opportunities to speak, ask questions, describe, explain their reasoning and make mistakes. Teaching subjects in Estonian requires teachers to set language-learning objectives alongside subject-specific goals and create opportunities to achieve them. Many teachers already have the methodological knowledge needed to do this. Yet when explaining more complex concepts, it may seem easier to switch to Russian. Students understand the material more quickly and the lesson can move forward.

But what happens when a teacher explains an entire topic in the students' native language, while the quiz or test must be completed in Estonian? Can we expect students to achieve a passing grade if they have not been taught the relevant Estonian vocabulary or given opportunities to use it?

In such cases, students may understand the subject matter perfectly well but struggle to understand the questions or formulate their answers. A poor result may therefore indicate a mismatch between the language of instruction and the language of assessment.

Are we grading knowledge of language proficiency?

Recent fourth-grade national assessments highlighted a contradiction in our education system. While the assessment of Estonian as a second language takes students' expected language proficiency into account, the same students faced significantly more complex vocabulary, lengthy texts and multipart questions in the natural science assessment.

Commenting on the linguistic complexity of the assessments, the Education and Youth Board (Harno) explained that the tasks are aligned with the curriculum and use the same terminology. If students' Estonian-language skills are insufficient, the agency recommends choosing the Russian-language assessment.

However, the Harno representative fails to consider that the students who took the natural science assessment have been studying subjects, including natural science, in Estonian for three years and may not even be familiar with the relevant terminology in Russian. I must admit that such a response is frustrating for teachers. Is recommending a Russian-language assessment really the solution to the challenges of transitioning to Estonian-language education?

Of course, students must also acquire subject-specific terminology in Estonian, but fair assessment means giving them an opportunity to demonstrate their actual knowledge and skills. That is precisely why, rather than simply recommending a switch of languages, we should also seek ways to make assessments in Estonian linguistically accessible to students.

Students cannot be responsible for adults' choices

A range of support measures have been established to facilitate the transition to Estonian-language education. Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) methodology centers operate at educational institutions, the Institute of the Estonian Language provides support through initiatives including the "Keelesamm" program and teachers in Tallinn can turn to the Tallinn Teachers' House and its methodology and competence center, MEKK. Teachers can attend training courses, receive guidance, explore teaching materials and learn from their colleagues' experiences. However, no trainer or methodology center can put what teachers have learned into practice in the classroom for them.

School leadership also has an important role to play. Schools must have a shared understanding of what Estonian-language education means and what principles should guide it. It is not enough for some teachers to consciously create an Estonian-language learning environment if others consistently switch to Russian during their lessons. Nor can the state's responsibility be limited to setting requirements. We need meaningful oversight that assesses whether Estonian-language education is actually working in practice.

Discussions about the transition to Estonian-language education often focus on students' lack of motivation, the language environment at home and parents' attitudes. These factors affect learning, but they cannot justify prejudging students' abilities.

Students do not choose their parents, the language spoken at home or their socioeconomic background. Teachers, however, can choose how they support students and what learning opportunities they provide. Students learning Estonian as a second language do not need lower expectations. They need high-quality teaching, consistent language support and teachers who believe in their abilities.

The transition to Estonian-language education is not simply about changing the language of instruction. Its goal must be to equip students with sufficient Estonian-language proficiency to continue their education, pursue their chosen field of study and compete on an equal footing with others in the future.

Achieving this requires effort from everyone involved. Students have a duty to learn, teachers have a responsibility to teach with clear intent, school leaders must establish shared principles and the state must ensure realistic expectations and meaningful oversight.

World.title: Gallery: Eesti 200 council meets to discuss party's future
World.content:
The council of the Eesti 200 party is meeting Sunday, with discussions focusing on the future of the party whose support is well below the electoral threshold ahead of the March 7 Riigikogu elections.

The agenda for the council meeting includes Eesti 200's future, preparations for the Riigikogu elections and a possible merger with the Estonian Greens, a party spokesperson said.

The meeting, held at the Õuetorn venue at the Telliskivi Creative Hub in Tallinn, began at 11 a.m. and is scheduled to end at 3 p.m.

Support for Eesti 200 has hovered around 2 percent in polls conducted by various polling firms for months. The party, which is currently in the governing coalition with the Reform Party, is divided over whether to take part in the March elections at all, run in alliance with the Greens or sit out this election cycle.

Fourteen MPs were elected to the Riigikogu on Eesti 200's list in the 2023 elections. Following the expulsion of Züleyxa Izmailova and the departure of Kalev Stoicescu, the party's parliamentary group now has 12 members.

According to the Business Register, the party had 548 members as of Sunday.

World.title: Expert: Trump's recent decisions have nothing to do with midterms
World.content:
Analyzing U.S. President Donald Trump's latest moves that have harmed Ukraine and favored Russia, U.S. politics expert Andreas Kaju admitted he could not explain why the president was making such decisions.

Fuel retailer Alexela's head of energy sales, Tarmo Kärsna, does not believe Russian diesel will help U.S. President Donald Trump achieve his goals of lowering fuel prices and saving American farmers.

"If Russian diesel were brought to the U.S. market, we would be talking about less than a day's consumption. It's a drop in the ocean. Markets are also skeptical today, questioning whether Russia even has the capacity to increase its diesel exports from their current level. After all, exports have fallen sevenfold since January of this year," Kärsna said.

The curtailment of Ukraine's satellite capabilities for striking Russia and defending itself, followed by the decision to abandon planned sanctions, are the latest surprises.

"It is clear that President Trump has taken Russia's side in the war and is clearly acting against Ukraine's interests. This is a very bad development," said European Parliament member Riho Terras (Isamaa).

Why? U.S. politics expert Andreas Kaju said he did not know. The midterm elections have nothing to do with it.

"If he wanted to win elections, he would have acted very differently long ago. What he has been doing consistently over the past year is endorsing extremely unpopular candidates within the Republican Party in various states. As a result, it is entirely possible that Republicans will lose states in the midterm elections that previously would have been unthinkable," Kaju said.

Kaju pointed to an article in the U.S. conservative publication National Review.

"The article argued that it is time for Republicans and Democrats to jointly launch a major congressional investigation into the reasons behind President Trump's Russia policy," Kaju said.

Kaju speculated that such investigations might indeed begin in Congress, including the Senate, after the midterm elections.

World.title: From spreadsheets to autonomous tractors: AI's growing role in farming
World.content:
Artificial intelligence primarily helps farmers process data in their daily operations, but autonomous agricultural robots and drones are no longer the stuff of science fiction either.

According to Airika Verrev, crop and livestock production manager and consultant at Pajo Ranch, AI's capabilities have improved significantly even in the short time she has been using it. This spring, the food producer tried using AI to compile data in Excel, but the technology was not yet up to the task. By the grain harvest season, however, that had changed.

"These days, I no longer create a single Excel spreadsheet myself. I tell AI what I want and what it should look like, and that's it," Verrev said.

She also uses AI to analyze data and find relevant provisions in legislation. Nevertheless, she said the information it provides must be constantly checked.

Marten Madissoo, assistant professor of agricultural engineering at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, confirmed that the technology does not relieve farmers of the responsibility to evaluate its answers.

"We have to bear in mind that AI is simply a useful tool that allows us to make decisions faster, but we still need to be experts ourselves," he said.

More broadly, Madissoo sees significant potential for machine learning and artificial intelligence in the agricultural sector. Potential applications include logistics, organizing the storage and processing of agricultural products and analyzing fields. However, he said there is no one-size-fits-all solution as the potential applications depend largely on the problem being addressed.

One possibility is to make better use of data that farmers already collect for field records, registers and reports.

"We have the advantage of having data spanning several years. By bringing this data together and developing a model to analyze it, we can achieve those gains," Madissoo said.

At the same time, he reiterated the need to combine agricultural and technical expertise. The relevant indicators must be assessed by people familiar with the fields who can define what they want to learn from the data.

From chat bots to field drones

However, chatbots are just the tip of the iceberg. Marten Madissoo coordinates the work of the AI and Robotics Center AIRE at the Estonian University of Life Sciences. The center focuses on opportunities to improve the competitiveness of industrial companies through artificial intelligence and robotics.

As an example of AI's industrial applications, Madissoo pointed to an AIRE demonstration project at meat producer Nõo Lihatööstus, which tested the use of AI for quality control of packaged products moving along a conveyor belt. The system was designed to detect problems such as poorly attached labels, incorrect dates or defects in a product's appearance.

Researchers at the University of Tartu have also used artificial intelligence to identify field islands in aerial photographs and sort grain. Novaator has previously reported on the Estonian University of Life Sciences' experiments with autonomous agricultural machinery.

The AgXeed AgBot autonomous tractor, jointly tested by the Estonian University of Life Sciences and Baltic Agro. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

New solutions involving agricultural drones could soon emerge. An amendment to the Plant Protection Act is currently being considered by the Riigikogu that would allow plant protection products to be sprayed from unmanned aircraft under certain conditions.

According to Madissoo, several autonomous solutions already exist, but their deployment is hindered by both legal restrictions and the need to ensure safety. For example, he said the Estonian University of Life Sciences' field robot is still firmly in the testing phase. The machine needs to be taught the boundaries of fields and where it can operate.

"It's not exactly science fiction, but it will still take some time before we can put all these technologies and capabilities to use," he said.

In his assessment, repetitive tasks with clearly defined procedures are particularly well suited to automation as machine learning can make them more efficient.

Trust but verify

Airika Verrev believes that, in the future, combining data with the help of AI will make farming significantly more precise. For example, AI could analyze aerial and drone photographs to help determine how much fertilizer or plant protection products need to be ordered for the upcoming season. This could help avoid unnecessary spending.

"The savings could actually be quite substantial. Right now, though, we're still estimating how much to order," she said.

According to Verrev, many producers currently use AI primarily as a more advanced search engine. However, she said a lack of time makes it difficult to keep up with new developments.

Madissoo said businesses' willingness to adopt new technology depends primarily on whether the benefits are clear and the investment is justified.

"How much do I need to invest and how quickly will that investment pay for itself?" he said, summing up the key question facing producers.

However, Madissoo believes that an initial experiment does not have to be expensive. Farmers can start with a chatbot and a specific question, then try analyzing their own data and testing the resulting recommendations on a smaller field, for example. For more complex ideas, he recommends seeking support from universities or AIRE.

"At one conference, someone gave a good example of AI adoption: Horses are still around today, but they have absolutely no significance in the transportation sector. It's the same with AI. You can manage without it, but you'll simply fall behind the mainstream. So I encourage people to use it: Trust, but verify," Madissoo said.

World.title: People increasingly not paying hospital fees
World.content:
Since patient visit fees increased last year, more and more people have been falling behind on payments to hospitals. Patients with outstanding debts can no longer see a specialist.

A year and a half ago, the cost of visiting a doctor quadrupled, with patient visit fees rising from €5 to €20 and daily hospital bed fees doubling from €2.50 to €5. Since then, the number of patients owing money to North Estonia Medical Center (PERH) has doubled, while the total amount owed has tripled.

"Daily hospital bed fees account for about 70 percent of the debt, while visit fees, mainly for emergency department visits, account for the remaining 30 percent," said Anneli Habicht, PERH's head of customer service.

According to Habicht, in about half of cases patients simply forget to pay, while the other half have no intention of paying. Before turning to a debt collection agency, the hospital spends a couple of months trying to recover the money itself.

"When we look at which groups are more likely to owe us money, it seems to be older people approaching retirement age, as well as very young adults. In terms of gender, men tend to be more likely to fall behind on payments," Habicht said.

Last year, nearly 2,200 people owed money to Narva Hospital. The amounts involved are generally small and are usually paid after a reminder.

"In the first nine months of this year, the number of debtors has increased by about 25 percent. At the same time, we haven't seen any behavior that would require us to take aggressive action through debt collection agencies or any signs that people are deliberately trying to avoid their obligations," said Narva Hospital CEO Üllar Lanno.

Tartu University Hospital has not experienced the same problems as its counterparts in northern Estonia.

"The hospital still receives most of its revenue for medical treatment through its contract with the Estonian Health Insurance Fund. Patients' out-of-pocket payments account for less than 3 percent of that. We have half a million outpatient visits a year and perhaps 200 to 400 patients need to be sent payment reminders," said Joel Starkopf, a member of Tartu University Hospital's management board.

According to debt collection agency Julianus Inkasso, the number of claims submitted by hospitals has increased by a few percentage points, although some medical institutions have submitted 10 percent more claims.

"When the visit fee was €5, it was a little easier to pay. If you're in a difficult financial situation, €20 is harder to afford. And if you forget to pay on time, finding that extra money later can be more difficult when you're working with a tight household budget," said Merle Laurimäe, CEO of Julianus Inkasso.

More than half of debtors settle their debts within a year of receiving a letter from the collection agency. However, they must also cover late-payment interest and collection fees of up to €30.

"I think the total could rise to around €55 at most, provided you act in time," Laurimäe said.

World.title: Reform Party unveils campaign slogan as PM touts economic growth
World.content:
Prime Minister and Reform Party chair Kristen Michal says Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average, as Reform pledges a clear course in the 2027 elections.

Speaking at the party's council meeting in Tartu on Saturday, Michal said the largest income tax cut in Estonia's history had doubled economic growth.

"Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average," he said, also citing rising wages, consumption, exports and manufacturing, alongside lower unemployment and easing inflation.

"The Reform Party can say with confidence: our plan is working," the prime minister emphasized. "Estonia has been led through a major test and is now on a solid growth path, moving forward even in the face of headwinds."

He noted that wages are rising, with consumer confidence up and people taking home an average of 10 percent more money this year. Defense spending of 5 percent GDP, he added, is also strengthening security and giving families and businesses confidence to plan for the future.

Even the opposition is starting to see that the Reform Party's plan is working, Michal said, accusing Isamaa and the Center Party of already making plans to form a coalition — potentially joined by the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE).

"The Reform Party is their main enemy for a reason: they can only steal Estonia's prosperity and growth if we're out of the picture," the party chair said, emphasizing that the key issue in the March 2027 elections will be whether this prosperity will continue to grow or be taken away from them.

Michal said that incomes must rise faster than prices, as a wealthier Estonia can invest more in education, healthcare, a cleaner environment and a better quality of life.

"No other party in Estonia stands as firmly for the economy, national defense, liberal principles, Estonian-language education and culture, and European values," he said. "These are the foundations of Estonia's future."

'A clear course for the future'

The Reform Party also unveiled its campaign slogan: "A clear course for the future."

Tartu mayor and party council chair Urmas Klaas said it reflects the party's focus on security, economic growth and opportunities for families and businesses.

He recalled that Reform's "Blue, black and white plan" for Estonia, unveiled in March, centers on building a stronger middle class, bolstering security and making greater use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the economy and government.



"We're running for election to ensure that robust security can give families confidence, people's work and knowledge can create prosperity and technology can help businesses grow and the state operate more efficiently," Klaas said.

MP and Reform Party secretary general Kristo Enn Vaga said the slogan emphasizes that Estonia's future is up to its own choices.

"We in the Reform Party want Estonia to be secure and the economy to grow, because that gives people and businesses more opportunities to carry out their plans," Vaga said. "This is the future we want to build."

World.title: Gallery: Public bomb shelter in Tallinn hidden behind woodland mural
World.content:
A street-level public civil defense shelter in the heart of downtown Tallinn has been transformed with a mural featuring Estonian trees and wildlife.

Located next to Kalev Sports Hall in Tiigiveski Park, the modular concrete shelter cannot withstand a direct missile hit, but it can protect around 20 people from blast waves, shrapnel and debris from an explosion as close as 50 meters away.

Similar shelters are already widely used in Ukraine, including in Kramatorsk.

The concrete module, donated by security company Citysec, is also now fully wrapped in a woodland mural by Colorees Art's Helena Hanni and Vahur Agar, featuring a wild hare, a bear family, an owl in flight and a wolf.

While usually kept closed in peacetime, the shelter was open to visitors on Friday, when officials were on hand to explain its features to the public.

Tallinn unveiled a new street-level civil defense shelter on Juhkentali tänav. October 2026. Source: Ellen Rudi/Tallinn Strategic Management Office

City weighs dozens more shelters

Citysec CEO Eduard Rikkas said the module was developed on a 50-50 basis with partners in Ukraine, where the design has already been in use for years.

Deputy Mayor Tiit Terik (Center) said the shelter door can be opened remotely during an emergency, and will unlock automatically if power or communications fail.

The shelter door, he added, will be kept locked in peacetime.

Tallinn has mapped 40 to 50 potential sites for similar shelters, with public procurement to follow if the city decides to order more.

According to the manufacturer, the shelter model installed on Juhkentali tänav costs up to €70,000.

World.title: US firms show increasing interest in developing Iraq’s hydrocarbon resources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Saturday that US firms are showing increasing interest in entering the Iraqi market and developing the country’s oil resources and petroleum industry.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), Khudair explained that the Iraqi government supports US corporations’ involvement in the Iraqi market, citing their significant expertise in the oil sector, as well as their ability to transfer knowledge to Iraqi staff.

Several American companies are operating in Iraq, including oil services and consulting firms such as Halliburton, Schlumberger, Baker Hughes, and KBR, according to Khudair. He indicated that the ministry reached agreements with Chevron, ExxonMobil, and ConocoPhillips.

Khudair clarified that the ministry is in negotiations with ExxonMobil to develop the Majnoon oil field, export infrastructure, and a seawater injection project with a capacity of 2.5 million barrels per day to maintain reservoir pressure.

The Iraqi oil minister noted that a deal with Halliburton has been activated to develop the Nahr Bin Umar and Sindbad fields. He added that an agreement with ConocoPhillips has been concluded to develop the Akkas gas field, where Schlumberger is currently operating the project’s first phase.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry activated a deal with Texas-based HKN to develop the Hamrin field, describing the agreement as significant since it develops both oil and gas resources.

Khudair further stated that the Oil Ministry encourages American and European enterprises and works to make the Iraqi market an appealing environment for them.

World.title: US lifts restrictions on Iraqi exchange firms
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed on Sunday that the US Treasury Department has lifted restrictions on several Iraqi exchange companies.

The CBI said in a statement that the US Treasury Department removed the restrictions after verifying that these companies met the standards it established, enabling them to resume the sale of US dollars to travelers.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen compliance with regulatory controls and organize the sale of foreign currency in accordance with approved frameworks, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

In late September, the spokesperson for the Iraqi government confirmed that Iraq received a new shipment of US dollars from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

Al-Aboudi explained that the step comes within the framework of bilateral understandings reached between Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and US officials during his recent visit to the United States.

The United States halted physical dollar supplies to Iraq in April 2026, including a huge cargo worth $500 million, to force Baghdad to limit the influence of Iran-backed armed groups and minimize illegal financial flow.

Washington decided to keep the supplies going in response to the Iraqi government’s efforts to tighten monitoring on dollar distribution, reduce currency abuse, expand electronic payments, and phase out the traditional currency auction system.

The revenues Iraq generates from international oil exports are officially stored in a designated account under the custody of the Federal Reserve Bank, giving Washington significant structural power over Baghdad’s access to physical cash.

The new funds will be used largely for travel-related activities and foreign transfers approved by the CBI.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister and UK National Security Adviser review security and economic ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi received British National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell in Baghdad on Sunday, October 18, 2026, to discuss expanding bilateral relations between Iraq and the United Kingdom, focusing particularly on defense coordination, intelligence sharing, and economic partnerships.

According to an official communique released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Powell extended congratulations to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi on the parliamentary confirmation and completion of his ministerial lineup.

The British envoy commended Baghdad’s ongoing anti-corruption campaign and structural economic reform agenda, affirming the United Kingdom’s backing for the Iraqi government’s institutional modernization and fiscal stabilization policies.

The discussions also addressed shifting geopolitical dynamics across the Middle East, with both sides underscoring the necessity of close multilateral coordination to de-escalate cross-border frictions.

The meeting emphasized joint diplomatic engagement to resolve underlying causes of regional instability, protect critical supply corridors, and anchor long-term security in the region.

World.title: Iraq’s oil output hits 4.4 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Eco Iraq, a digital platform that analyzes economic, energy, and environmental data in the country, revealed on Saturday that oil production during September reached its highest daily average since the beginning of 2026, at 4.39 million barrels per day.

According to the observatory, Iraq’s oil output stayed at normal levels in January and February, averaging more than 4.1 million barrels per day, before falling drastically in March as a result of the military conflict in the Middle East.

Oil output fell to its lowest point in May before gradually recovering in the months that followed.

Iraq’s average daily oil output was 4.09 million barrels in January and 4.14 million barrels in February before falling to 1.9 million barrels in March and 1.63 million in April.

In May, the country’s oil production fell to 1.4 million barrels per day before rising to 1.52 million in June.

The improvement in oil output continued until the third quarter of the year. According to figures from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), average output increased to 2.9 million barrels per day in July, 3.74 million barrels per day in August, and 4.39 million barrels per day in September.

Iraq’s oil production in September reached its highest daily rate since the beginning of 2026, signaling a gradual recovery in output following the sharp decline experienced during the months of war in the region.

World.title: Iraq to appoint Al Halbousi and Al Fayyadh as Vice Presidents
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi political factions within the governing State Administration Coalition have reached a preliminary agreement to reactivate the long-dormant positions of Vice President of the Republic, an informed political source revealed on Sunday, October 18, 2026.

Under the emerging cross-party consensus, the leadership posts are slated to be assigned to Taqaddum Party leader and former Parliament Speaker Mohammed Al-Halbousi alongside Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Falih Al-Fayyadh.

According to the source, the prospective appointments will mirror the financial compensation model adopted for deputy prime ministers, restricting allocations solely to nominal salary entitlements without authorizing supplementary office operational budgets or creating new civil service staff quotas.

The financial restraint is designed to forestall public criticism and prevent administrative expansion within executive payrolls while accommodating broad-based political power-sharing requirements across key coalition partners.

The source noted that restoring the two vice-presidential slots has featured prominently across bilateral consultations and plenary coalition assemblies as a stabilizing mechanism for the current parliamentary cycle.

The political maneuvering follows action taken by the Council of Representatives on Thursday, October 15, when lawmakers ratified three deputy prime ministers and filled eleven ministerial portfolios—including vacant and newly established ministries—within Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s cabinet, while deferring a vote on the Ministry of Migration and Displaced.

World.title: Central Bank of Iraq raises housing loan allocations to 3 trillion dinars
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) announced on Sunday, October 18, 2026, an expansion of its financial allocations supporting the national housing sector, increasing the designated lending portfolio to three trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $1.97 billion).

The initiative is aimed directly at addressing the high volume of citizen applications seeking to purchase apartments and residential units inside organized housing complexes across Iraqi governorates.

According to an official administrative directive issued by the Central Bank, the decision is enacted pursuant to the provisions of CBI Law No. 56 of 2004, as amended.

The measure triples the previous funding ceiling specified in a prior regulatory directive dated August 22, 2024, raising the aggregate financing cap from one trillion dinars to three trillion dinars while retaining the existing operational terms, repayment criteria, and credit conditions.

The directive instructed the Director General of the relevant specialized lending institution to visit the Central Bank’s headquarters in Baghdad to formally sign the contractual annex required for the allocation increase and finalize administrative protocols.

The liquidity injection expands mortgage-backed real estate credit, stimulates the domestic construction industry, and bridges the acute housing deficit by enabling middle-income citizens to secure homeownership inside modern investment residential compounds.

World.title: PMF’s ammunition depot explodes in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered investigation into the circumstances surrounding an explosion at an ammunition depot in a Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) base in the capital, Baghdad, according to the Iraqi Security Media Cell (ISMC).

Al-Zaidi stressed the need to expedite the investigation to find out the specific reasons for the incident and implement all essential safety measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.

The PMF announced on Saturday that five of its members had been wounded following an explosion at an ammunition depot located at one of its bases in eastern Baghdad.

The PMF confirmed in a statement that a fire—triggered by the explosion of a stockpile of damaged ammunition at one of its headquarters in eastern Baghdad—has been brought under control.

The statement indicated that the explosion caused minor injuries to five personnel. Specialized committees have initiated an investigation into the incident’s causes, and the findings will be announced upon the investigation’s conclusion.

During the early stages of the military conflict in the Middle East, which has spilled over into Iraq, several PMF headquarters were targeted in devastating bombings carried out by the United States.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt discuss electricity interconnection project through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed on Saturday approaches to expedite the electricity interconnection project between Egypt, Iraq, and Jordan.

According to a statement released by the Egyptian Foreign Ministry, the meeting took place during Abdelatty’s visit for the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers and ahead of al-Zaidi’s scheduled trip to Egypt on November 23.

The meeting addressed measures to improve bilateral cooperation, as well as attempts to de-escalate tensions in the region and promote security and stability.

The two sides discussed the activation of the three countries’ trilateral cooperation mechanism and strategies to advance collaborative projects, notably in electricity interconnection and oil, to promote economic integration and serve the three nations’ common interests.

Abdelatty emphasized the necessity of boosting economic, commercial, and investment relations with Iraq, notably by increasing Egyptian firms’ participation in infrastructure, reconstruction, and development projects.

The Egyptian foreign minister emphasized the possibilities for utilizing Egyptian experience in construction, transportation, energy, agriculture, and pharmaceutical industries.

Abdelatty highlighted the importance of increasing bilateral commerce and facilitating Egyptian products’ access to the Iraqi market.

Additionally, Abdelatty underlined Egypt’s unwavering support for Iraq’s unity, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, opposing foreign involvement in its internal affairs.

The Egyptian foreign minister also praised the Iraqi government’s efforts to improve national security and reinforce state authority and institutions, including bringing arms under state control.

World.title: Espionage case on Army officer’s wife, lens on ‘China links’
World.content:
JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a case and started a probe against a Jammu-based Army officerâs wife for allegedly collecting and sharing sensitive information with foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, sources said Sunday.

The woman is from Telangana, works as a freelance researcher and had a UN internship in 2023. She allegedly used AI tools ChatGPT and Claude to write papers on sensitive security issues for Chinese intelligence operatives suspected to have contacted her posing as academicians. The information was allegedly passed on through encrypted communication (online) mediums.

The woman married the major-rank officer in 2023, a year after finishing a course in international governance from Geneva.

She got a Masterâs degree from a Bengaluru university in 2021.

A joint team of officers, including some from a central intelligence agency, intercepted the woman at Jammu railway station on Oct 14 when she was reportedly preparing to board a train to Pathankot. She was stopped and taken to a nearby military station for questioning, officials said. This followed a case filed at Jammuâs Gandhi Nagar Police Station under Official Secrets Act, and BNS sections relating to criminal conspiracy and offences against national sovereignty.





A DSP assigned to lead the probe has questioned the woman, seizing her phone and extracting data that purportedly showed documents on sensitive subjects. The accused claimed her material was based entirely on open-source research supplemented by the AI platforms.

The officials made it clear that despite being booked, the woman has not been arrested yet. Her interrogation indicated that she had interacted with several foreign nationals during her UN internship, including a Chinese national with whom she allegedly maintained contact through WhatsApp, the officials said.

In 2024, she was in contact via social media with a Malaysian consultant allegedly working for Chinese intelligence agencies, the officials added.

Preliminary investigations indicate the Chinese operatives initially made the woman write articles on environmental and geopolitics issues before gradually goading her to switch to defence matters. Investigators suspect she may have fallen into an âintellectual trapâ, not realising that those approaching her as academicians were actually operatives trying to extract sensitive information.

World.title: Almost a century after J&K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Almost a century after the establishment of Jammu & Kashmir HC, the Union Territory of Ladakh Sunday got a high court bench, which will sit in Leh, 3,500 metres above sea level â an altitude no other HC can ever match.

Inaugurating the Ladakh bench of J&K HC, CJI Surya Kant said, âI am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves.â

J&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein.

Speaking on the evolution of the justice delivery system in Ladakh in the presence of HC Chief Justice Pushpendra Kumar Bhati and SC judges, CJI Kant said given the difficult terrain and harsh winter, approaching the court was more arduous than the cost of litigation for many.

Only after Ladakh became a UT in 2019 was J&K HC rechristened HC of J&K and Ladakh.

âBut a name on a courtâs letterhead is not the same as a court on oneâs doorstepâ¦ The high court has today crossed the passes to reach Ladakh, instead of asking the people of Ladakh to cross the passes to reach it,â he said, appreciating the efforts of Union govt and Lt Governor V K Saxena, who was present at the ceremony along with attorney general R Venkataramani.





But even establishing an HC bench at Leh would not take justice to the doorstep of far-flung villages in the region, the CJI said, advocating liberal use of technology and legal aid services.

âAccess to justice, after all, begins not in the courtâs compound, but at the litigantâs door. The law places this duty on the HC as well, through its legal services committee, and I am confident that, working... with the legal services authority, it will discharge that responsibility by reaching every door in Ladakh where justice is still awaited,â he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In an unprecedented gesture, the CJI said, âOnce video-conferencing facilities are adequately available to the lawyers of the Ladakh bench, Supreme Court shall list all matters coming from Ladakh on a single day, and hear them on a day-to-day basis, also through videoconferencing.â

âSomewhere in Ladakh today, in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra, there is a young child who will one day argue her first case in this court, and perhaps even sit on its bench as a judge. When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh but taken root here,â the CJI said.

World.title: ‘Should focus on actual criminals’: Dipke jabs police after shots fired at Tiger Shroff
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke took a jibe on the government and police, accusing them of having their priorities misplaced, after the recent firing on actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai on Sunday.

âInstead of cracking down on students and activists, the police should focus on actual criminals,â Dipke said in a post on X.

Dipke had previously tweeted his frustration, accusing the state of intentionally prolonging Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's arrest in order to delay court proceedings and delay their release.

âThis is what happens when the Govt and police have their priorities completely misplaced,â Dipke said.

Tiger Shroffâ car was fired upon by three motorcycle-borne assailants around 7 pm. The attack injured his driver and a nearby fan hoping to catch his glimpse

According to Juhu police, Shroff had attended a birthday celebration at Pushpa Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, and was preparing to leave when the firing took place. The three assailants, who were dressed in white shirts, fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station.

The firing took place around 350 metres from Juhu police station and Pushpa Park. Shroff's driver, Firdosh, sustained a bullet injury to his left hand and was taken to Nanavati Hospital.

Tiger has never publicly expressed his opinions regarding Dipke or his CJP.

Police are examining a social media post in which Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu purportedly took responsibility for the attack.

While rumours linked Pandit to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, police had yet to verify the authenticity of the post.

World.title: 'Barged in, cut power': AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj claims Delhi Police harassing Bengali community in CR Park
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Saurabh Bharadwaj has accused Delhi Police of harassing the Bengali community and Durga Puja committees in Chittaranjan Park (CR Park), alleging that police personnel forcibly disconnected electricity at a pandal and damaged equipment.

He also warned that restrictions on Puja celebrations could lead to overcrowding, drawing a parallel with the Kolkata stampede that killed 17 people on Saturday.

In a post on X addressed to Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) state president claimed that the community and Puja organisers were facing unprecedented harassment.

âAttention @LtGovDelhi saab, Delhi Police officers are harassing the Bengali community and CR Park Durga Puja Committees like never before.

This community is one of the most decent and well-educated sections of Delhi,â he wrote.

Questioning the alleged disparity in the treatment of different cultural events, Bharadwaj referred to the Delhi government's position on allowing shops and businesses to operate round the clock and said most Ram Leela celebrations were permitted to continue past midnight.

âWhen the Delhi Govt talks about 24x7 businesses and shops, and most Ram-leelas are allowed past midnight, why the stepmotherly treatment for the Bengali community?â he asked.





Bharadwaj also alleged that police constables entered the B Block Durga Puja pandal on Saturday and cut its electricity connections. âYesterday, police constables barged into the B Block Durga Puja pandal and forcibly cut the electrical connections, damaging their equipment. This is not done,â he said.

In another post on X, Bharadwaj criticised the BJP over the reported West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy and raised concerns about crowd management at the Puja pandals.

âBJP has learnt nothing from the West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy,â he wrote.

He claimed that lakhs of people, including Bengalis and non-Bengalis, visit CR Park's Puja pandals every year, particularly in the evenings. He further alleged that Puja committees had been told that pandals and loudspeakers could operate only until 10 pm this year, compared with midnight last year.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âSqueezing the evening window by 2 hours will cause crowd swell and chaos.

This could lead to a West Bengal-type situation, and the government will prosecute puja committees to hide its own shortcomings,â Bharadwaj alleged.

Meanwhile, the Delhi Traffic Police has announced restrictions in CR Park, Greater Kailash-II and adjoining areas of South Delhi from October 16 to 20, between 4 pm and midnight, citing the expected influx of visitors and limited road space around the pandals.

Private vehicles belonging to visitors and devotees will not be allowed to enter CR Park and Greater Kailash-II during the restricted hours. Commuters have been advised to use the Delhi Metro, with taxi and auto-rickshaw drop-off points designated at Greater Kailash and Nehru Enclave Metro stations. The police has also warned that illegally parked vehicles or those obstructing traffic may be towed and prosecuted.

The restrictions are scheduled to remain in place until October 20.

World.title: Bimol Akoijam willing to contest Manipur Assembly polls if Congress offers ticket
World.content:
File photo: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam

JNU dismissal and police investigation

Akoijam says Manipur's wider crisis needs attention

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam on Sunday said he was willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from the Keishamthong constituency if the party offered him a ticket, as he faces a sexual harassment case and has been dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).Speaking at an event, the Inner Manipur MP said his decision to enter the electoral contest would be guided by the future of the state."I am ready to fight elections from Keishamthong (in Imphal West district). If the party offers me a ticket, I will contest the Keisamthong assembly constituency. This decision is for the future of the state," Akoijam said, according to news agency PTI.The Manipur Assembly elections are due next year.His remarks come amid an ongoing police investigation into sexual harassment allegations against him and his dismissal from JNU, where he was a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences.Akoijam was dismissed from the university on October 9 following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment. He has denied the charges and described the university's action as a "witch hunt", claiming he was not given an opportunity to respond to the inquiry committee's findings.Delhi Police booked him on October 11 following a complaint by JNU's chief security officer. He recently appeared before investigators at the Vasant Kunj North Police Station in New Delhi in connection with the case.At least 11 female students submitted complaints against Akoijam in May. They alleged that he invited students to his campus residence on the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to harass them. Some students also alleged that he made obscene and inappropriate remarks in class.After appearing before investigators, Akoijam said he intended to challenge his dismissal legally.Speaking to reporters in Imphal on Friday, he said his lawyers were preparing the case and that he would file it within a day or two.He also said he had cooperated with the police and would continue to do so, while requesting adequate notice for any further questioning because of his responsibilities as an MP.During his remarks to the media, Akoijam also urged greater attention to the wider situation in Manipur, including the plight of internally displaced people, lawlessness and issues surrounding buffer zones."Thousands of people are languishing in relief camps. I donât think my pain is anything greater than the pain of these people," he said, while alleging that the action against him was an attempt to silence his voice.The MP had earlier said, "Justice will be done," before travelling to New Delhi to join the police investigation.The allegations have also triggered political reactions in the state. BJP workers staged a protest outside Congress Bhavan in Imphal, demanding Akoijam's resignation and accusing him of bringing disrepute to Manipur. Police prevented the protesters from entering the premises.Congress spokesperson Hareshwar Goshwami described the protest as a diversionary tactic and accused the ruling party of deflecting attention from killings and the crisis in the state.Akoijam has maintained that the allegations against him are false and has challenged the process that led to his dismissal. The sexual harassment allegations remain under investigation.

World.title: Global uranium production to dip by 50% by 2040 as demand set to double, says IAEA report; forecast could pinch India too
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Global uranium supply constraints would witness mining production drop by at least 50% by 2040 even as demand is set to double, according to the latest International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) report.

This IAEA forecast on global uranium supply crunch is likely to affect Indiaâs goal to increase its nuclear capacity to 100 GW by 2047.

According to publication âUranium 2024: Resources, Production and Demandâ, also known as the âRed Bookâ, jointly prepared by Nuclear Energy Agency of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and the Agency, global uranium requirements are projected to increase to 90,045 tonnes of uranium (tU) in the low-case scenario and up to 1,42,631 tU in the high-case scenario by 2050, which represents a 50% to 144% increase from todayâs requirements of approximately 60,000 tU.

In contrast to future doubling of uranium requirements, uranium production from existing mines is forecast to decrease by at least 50% by 2040, the report said. âConversion capacity is already insufficient and is projected to fall further behind demand through 2040, highlighting the need for substantial new investment and facility expansions. While global enrichment capacity currently exceeds demand, it remains unevenly distributed geographically,â it said.





The report suggested new mines and expansion or life extension of existing mines, as well as reopening of idled mines, saying these steps will be required for assurance of supply in the future.

Amid the gloomy scenario predicted by IAEA, India has initiated steps to increase nuclear power capacity from current 8,180 MW to 22,480 MW by 2031-32. The expansion includes construction and commissioning of 10 reactors, totalling 8,000 MW, across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Karnataka, and MP.

Additionally, pre-project activities for 10 more reactors have commenced, with plans for progressive completion by 2031-32.

Further, the Modi govt accorded in-principle approval to set up 6 x 1208 MW nuclear power plant in cooperation with the USA at Kovvada in Srikakulam district in Andhra Pradesh.

India procures uranium from a combination of domestic mining and international suppliers: Domestic uranium is mined by Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) from deposits in Jharkhand, Andhra and Karnataka.

It relies primarily on natural uranium for its pressurised heavy water reactors and is gradually shifting toward a closed fuel cycle using plutonium-fuelled fast breeder reactors (FBRs) and eventually thorium.

To supplement limited domestic reserves and back its expansion targets under HANTI Act, 2025, India imports and has active supply arrangements with Kazakhstan, Russia, Canada, Australia (finalised arrangements under a nuclear cooperation deal), Uzbekistan and France.

However, the IAEA prediction of uranium shortfall if drastic steps not taken could pinch India too.

Over the next decade, nuclear fuel production will face increasing demand across all nuclear fuel-related segments due to increasing construction programmes in both established and embarking countries, necessitating the development of new fuel types, including for small modular reactors and advanced reactors, it said.

âAn increase in uranium production will require sustained investment with positive market conditions, and the discovery of new deposits will require sustained long-term exploration efforts, bearing in mind that the development of new uranium mines takes 10â15 years on average, from deposit discovery to the start of mining operations,â it said.

In addition, significant and timely investment in exploration and mining/processing technology will be required, including cost-effective uranium extraction techniques for exploiting unconventional deposit types (for example uranium from phosphate and black shale deposits), some of which may become economic if there is a sustained increase in market prices, it suggested.

World.title: Centre issues advisory to Meta, asks it to overhaul content promotion system on Facebook, Instagram
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives.

"

"Ensure that recommendation systems do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives, and endeavour to provide appropriate diversity of relevant and credible information," an advisory issued by the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), dated October 10, stated, PTI reported.

"Also strengthen mechanisms for rapid identification, review and escalation of content, which is gaining significant reach through recommendation systems and has the potential to cause widespread public confusion, apprehension, violence or disturbance of public order," it added.

While the advisory does not cite any specific incident that led to its issuance, it comes amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

MeitY also asked Meta to cooperate with law enforcement and other authorised government agencies by providing information or assistance within the timelines prescribed under the IT Rules, 2021.





The ministry noted that certain content relating to "ongoing public events" was being "prominently displayed and recommended to users" on Meta platforms.

Citing the Information Technology Act, 2000, the advisory highlighted the companyâs obligation to exercise due diligence under the IT Rules, 2021, which require intermediaries to inform users about prohibited content, including material likely to cause public disorder or incite a cognisable offence.

MeitY also flagged content presenting old or selectively edited visuals as current events, misleading claims about emergencies, restrictions or police action, and audio-visual material depicting law-and-order situations without adequate context. It also raised concerns over content likely to incite violence and misleading material receiving disproportionate amplification.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The advisory outlined six requirements for Meta, including measures to identify and address prohibited content and review recommendation and ranking systems to ensure misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not "disproportionately amplified or repeatedly recommended to users".

MeitY emphasised that the advisory seeks to promote responsible information dissemination while respecting lawful expression and public discourse.

"Meta is advised to ensure that any action taken pursuant to this advisory is consistent with the Information Technology Act, 2000, the IT Rules, 2021, and other applicable laws," the ministry added.

World.title: Agha's comeback century sinks Sri Lanka and gives Pakistan winning start in tri-series
World.content:
Salman Ali Agha made a triumphant return to the Pakistan team with his fourth ODI century in a 37-run victory over Sri Lanka in the cricket tri-series opener on Sunday (October 18, 2026).

Agha hit 107 off 90 balls, and Pakistan scored 305 all out in 49.5 overs after Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won his fourth successive toss and chose to field.

Agha was among seven Pakistan cricketers summoned back home at the end of August during a tumultuous tour of England after Agha had led the team in the first test.

Pakistan pace bowlers overcame heavy dew and threatening half centuries from Pavan Rathnayake (79) and Janith Liyanage (60) to dismiss Sri Lanka for 268 in 48.1 overs.

Captain Shaheen Afridi picked up 3-55 while Naseem Shah pinned down Sri Lanka's top-order with impressive swing bowling to finish with 2-43. Haris Rauf ran through the tail with 2-48 while seam all-rounder Faheem Ashraf grabbed 2-49, including the key wicket of Rathnayake.

Pakistan will play England in Rawalpindi on Tuesday (October 20) in the second match of the tri-series.

Sri Lanka struggles against paceAvishka Fernando, making a comeback to ODIs, top-edged Shah while Kusal Mendis struggled for 34 balls to score only 18 before he fell to Ashraf.

Kamindu Mendis (44 in 50) survived two dropped catches before Afridi struck twice in his return spell as Sri Lanka limped to 91-4 in the 20th over of its chase.

Rathnayake and Liyanage then revived Sri Lankan hopes with a 119-run stand with Pakistan pacers unable to reverse swing the wet ball due to heavy dew at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. But the dismissal of Rathnayake in the 38th over provided Pakistan an opening despite Dasun Shanaka, playing his first ODI since the start of 2024, scoring 28 off 18 balls.

Agha revives Pakistan

After being summoned home, Agha was later not only removed as Pakistan T20 captain but also lost his place in the T20 team that beat Sri Lanka 2-1 in the recent three-match series. However, Agha scored prolifically in domestic cricket, including a triple century and forced his way back into the ODI side.

Agha revived Pakistan from 118-4 in the 22nd over with partnerships with Hasan Nawaz (37) and Arafat Minhas (18) before Sri Lanka hit back in the death overs.

Eshan Malinga (4-46) and Asitha Fernando (3-59) denied Pakistan a big finish in the final five overs with multiple strikes as Pakistan, at 279-5, went on to lose its last five wickets for 26 runs. Malinga bowled a double-wicket maiden over before No. 11 Haris Rauf denied him a hat trick.

Dilshan Madushanka (2-67) removed openers Fakhar Zaman (16) and Saim Ayub (7) in his opening spell.

Babar Azam and 19-year-old debutant Saad Baig rebuilt with a 74-run third-wicket stand before Malinga removed both batters in successive overs.

Babar, who has scored just one ODI hundred in more than two years, fell for 45 off 57 balls when he pulled Malinga's short ball to mid-wicket. Baig smashed two sixes and three fours before he too was tempted to pull Malinga and holed out at deep fine leg.

Agha snatched the momentum from Sri Lanka with a 97-run stand with Nawaz. The only specialist leg-spinner Sachindu Colombage (0-61) struggled as Agha completed his half century off 48 balls and Nawaz also opened up against the leg-spinner.

Fernando returned and broke the partnership when Nawaz was well caught by Rathnayake over his head at mid-wicket. Agha continued to bat aggressively in a 64-run stand with Minhas before raising his hundred with an edged boundary.

World.title: Union Minister meets start-up leaders over NCR pollution
World.content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav, on Saturday interacted with representatives of start-ups and innovation companies working on air pollution mitigation, with a focus on developing practical, scalable and technology-driven solutions to address the air pollution challenge in Delhi-NCR.

Innovative approaches for low-cost mechanised road sweeping, monitoring road-dust resuspension, portable pothole repair and modular dust-containment systems were also discussed.

The Minister informed that the main focus of the interaction was on using artificial intelligence, sensors, remote sensing, satellite and drone-based technologies and data analytics to move towards real-time understanding of air pollution. He said that solutions presented by the innovators include hyperlocal air-quality monitoring, city-wide pollution mapping, hotspot identification and forecasting, AI-based source apportionment, real-time identification of pollution sources and predictive traffic-congestion management.

Technologies were displayed for 24x7 detection of stubble and open biomass burning, as well as automated identification of vehicles without valid PUC (Pollution Under Control) certificates and over-aged vehicles, which could further strengthen timely enforcement and intervention, he added.

Some of these companies are already working with different government bodies and more are expected to work with the government in different levels in the coming months, an official said.

World.title: Expired products, pests found at online food delivery stores in Delhi
World.content:
Ahead of the festival season, the Food Safety Department found expired products, pests and unhygienic storage conditions at facilities operated by quick-commerce and retail companies in various parts of Delhi. It also tested samples of different brands of desi ghee sold in markets across the city. Of the 59 samples tested, 19 were found to be “unsafe” for human consumption, while four failed to meet food safety standards, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) stated in an official release on Saturday. According to the CMO, officials found expired frozen green peas, Greek yoghurt, eggless chocolate-chip brownies and cow ghee products at Swiggy Instamart’s premises in Uttam Nagar. Some packets of sprouts, fruits and vegetables also did not carry expiry dates. At Reliance Retail Limited’s premises in the Wazirpur Industrial Area, flies, mosquitoes and a lizard were found, along with spider webs. During an inspection at Zomato Hyperpure’s premises in Ghevra, officials found expired products and unhygienic conditions. At Zepto Limited’s premises in Jheel Khureja, shortcomings were found in maintaining the prescribed cold-storage temperature. Cockroaches and spider webs were also found, the statement said.

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said compromising on food quality or endangering people’s health through adulteration was unacceptable under any circumstances.

“The health and safety of Delhiites will not be compromised. The Food Safety Department has been directed to tighten monitoring of markets, food storage facilities and establishments supplying food products through online platforms. Action must be taken in accordance with the rules wherever food safety standards are violated,” Ms. Gupta said.

Unsafe ghee

The Food Safety Department collected 59 samples of different brands of desi ghee from markets across Delhi. “Samples of 19 brands were declared ‘unsafe for human consumption’, including Haryana Lite, Haryana Supreme, Haryana Dairy, Haryana Pure, Shree Haryana King, Shree Haryana Foods, Kartar, Prabhas, Madhu Sangam, Radha Krishna, New Punjab Super Brand, Akshara, Anand Gold, Shree Nandan, Shree Mohan and Shree Krishna,” the statement said. “Samples of Nova, Govardhan Pure Cow Ghee and Pratap Desi Ghee were classified as substandard. Orders have been issued to shut down establishments selling unsafe ghee, and their licences have been suspended,” it added. Ms. Gupta said the government’s objective was not merely to identify deficiencies but to ensure that every family in Delhi had access to safe and quality food. Protecting public health and ensuring accountability in the food trade remained government priorities, she added.

World.title: ‘Forcibly removed’: Jamia students staging hunger strike face rustication, campus ban
World.content:
Students on hunger strike demanding the restoration of Jamia Millia Islamia’s students’ union elections alleged they were “forcibly removed” from the protest site around 5.30 a.m. on Saturday, triggering further protests. The administration, however, denied using force and said the students were asked to vacate the spot as they were protesting outside the designated area.

Several students have been staging a hunger strike since October 12 demanding the restoration of student union elections that were last held in 2006.

The university authorities initiated disciplinary action against two students, who initiated the strike. On Saturday, Ebin Basil, the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) unit general secretary at JMI, said he received a one-year rustication notice while Jasim Ali, a postgraduate student, got a six-month campus ban order.

The Jamia unit of the NSUI, in a statement, said, “Approximately 60 security guards, accompanied by the chief proctor and security advisor, arrived at the protest site and forcibly dragged away the students.”

Students ‘detained’

Students also alleged that at least 12 protesters were detained by the police while staging a demonstration against their forcible removal.

However, a senior police officer said they were “removed” from the campus gate for “destroying public property” and released in the evening without any charges.

The administration announced that the campus will remain closed for five days to celebrate the upcoming festivals.

‘Supressing dissent’

The action comes amid growing concern among Delhi students over a shrinking space for dissent. Activists have highlighted the recent denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site, daily detentions, and the imposition of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) across parts of the capital.

JMI has not held student union elections since 2006, when they were dissolved following campus violence. A university spokesperson said, “We have received no written representation regarding the matter. Over the years, elections have evolved and we conduct department-centric student elections, which have served the campus well.”

Last year, a controversy erupted in February when 14 students were detained by the police from inside the campus for allegedly vandalising public property and disturbing law and order. The students were protesting against administrative clampdowns on democracy and freedom of speech inside the campus.

Since then, the university has doubled down on protests on campus. In October last year, the university earmarked one spot near gate number 18 as the designated protest site, leaving the rest of campus “out of bounds” for protests.

(With inputs from Lavpreet Kaur)
